metas.titre: Phase III Prospective Randomised Study of Netarsudil and Concomitant Latanoprost Efficacy and Safety for Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma or Ocular Hypertension in Japan: J-ROCKET-2.
metas.texte:
Phase III Prospective Randomised Study of Netarsudil and Concomitant Latanoprost Efficacy and Safety for Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma or Ocular Hypertension in Japan: J-ROCKET-2.. INTRODUCTION: This prospective, phase III, randomised, multicentre, double-masked study (jRCT2031210122) assessed the intraocular pressure (IOP)-lowering efficacy, tolerability and superiority of netarsudil 0.02% + concomitant latanoprost 0.005% to placebo + latanoprost in Japanese participants with primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) or ocular hypertension (OHT) who have inadequate IOP reduction with latanoprost monotherapy.
METHODS: Participants received latanoprost once daily for 6 weeks. Secondary endpoints included MD IOP at weeks 1 and 2. Adverse events (AEs) were recorded.

metas.titre: Is the interventional glaucoma paradigm reflected in real-world practice? Insights from iStent combined with cataract surgery (2010-2022).
metas.texte: Is the interventional glaucoma paradigm reflected in real-world practice? Insights from iStent combined with cataract surgery (2010-2022).. PurposeTo analyze trends in the clinical use of the iStent device, characterize the evolving baseline profile of treated patients, and assess surgical outcomes over time.MethodsThis retrospective longitudinal study included 145 eyes undergoing iStent implantation between 2010 and 2022. Data included intraocular pressure (IOP), medications, and functional and structural parameters. Surgical success was defined using three criteria: (1) IOP <21 mmHg with medication reduction, (2) IOP <18 mmHg with medication reduction, and (3) IOP <21 mmHg with a ≥ 20% reduction from baseline.ResultsiStent use increased from 3.4% to 9.4% of glaucoma surgeries (p = 0.0125). metas.titre: Efficacy and safety of netarsudil compared with prostaglandin-based therapies: a Bayesian network meta-analysis.
metas.texte: Efficacy and safety of netarsudil compared with prostaglandin-based therapies: a Bayesian network meta-analysis.. The study aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of netarsudil (NET), alone or in fixed-dose combinations (FDC), in comparison with prostaglandin analogues (PGAs: bimatoprost [BIM], latanoprost [LAT], travoprost [TRA], and tafluprost [TAF]) for the treatment of primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) or ocular hypertension. Literature search in PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science (inception to July 2025). Identified 26 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) (5,390 patients). The primary outcome was the mean difference in intraocular pressure (IOP) reduction at 3 months; the secondary outcome was the incidence of conjunctival hyperemia. Pair-wise meta-analysis used Cochrane Review Manager 5.4, Bayesian network meta-analysis via Aggregate Data Drug Information System (ADDIS) with Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) simulations. Inconsistency assessed via node-splitting, convergence evaluated via Brooks-Gelman-Rubin method. Network meta-analysis showed 3-month IOP -lowering hierarchy: FDC > BIM > TRA > LAT > TAF > NET. metas.titre: Intrapapillary Damage and Its Functional Association in Normal Tension Glaucomatous Eyes With and Without Peripapillary Intrachoroidal Cavitation.
metas.texte:
Intrapapillary Damage and Its Functional Association in Normal Tension Glaucomatous Eyes With and Without Peripapillary Intrachoroidal Cavitation.. PURPOSE: To compare optic nerve head (ONH) structure, visual field (VF) characteristics, and structure-function relationships including intrapapillary structural changes between normal tension glaucomatous (NTG) eyes with and without peripapillary intrachoroidal cavitation (PICC).
METHODS: This cross-sectional observational study enrolled 94 NTG eyes with PICC (NTG + PICC), 188 NTG eyes without PICC (NTG - PICC) matched for age, axial length, and VF severity, and 30 healthy eyes. Bruch's membrane opening (BMO) and scleral flange opening (SFO) were identified on ONH-centered OCT images. SFO-minimum rim width (SFO-MRW), the shortest distance between the SFO and prelaminar tissue surface, was used to evaluate focal intrapapillary tissue thinning. ONH structure, sectoral Humphrey 24-2 VF sensitivity (VFS), circumpapillary retinal nerve fiber layer thickness and SFO-MRW were compared among groups. metas.titre: Multi-omics identification and verification of Dnajb14 as a modulator of retinal ganglion cell survival in glaucoma through ferroptosis.
metas.texte: Multi-omics identification and verification of Dnajb14 as a modulator of retinal ganglion cell survival in glaucoma through ferroptosis.. Glaucoma is a leading cause of irreversible blindness and necessitates the identification of unreported therapeutic targets. Here, we report eight stable plasma protein targets for glaucoma, identified through a large-scale proteome-wide association study integrated with Mendelian randomization and colocalization analyses. Among these candidates, we show that the DnaJ heat shock protein family member B14 (DNAJB14) acts as a critical neuroprotective factor. Using single-cell and bulk transcriptomics, we demonstrate that Dnajb14 is characteristically expressed in retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and that its abundance is inversely correlated with ferroptosis under ischemic stress. Furthermore, our results reveal that Dnajb14 preserve RGC survival and structural and functional integrity in multiple acute and chronic murine models. metas.titre: A Multimodal Approach to Open-Angle Glaucoma with Travoprost Intracameral Implant and Minimally Invasive Glaucoma Surgery with or Without Concurrent Cataract Surgery.
metas.texte:
A Multimodal Approach to Open-Angle Glaucoma with Travoprost Intracameral Implant and Minimally Invasive Glaucoma Surgery with or Without Concurrent Cataract Surgery.. INTRODUCTION: This study aimed to characterize reductions in intraocular pressure (IOP) and the need for topical IOP-lowering medications in eyes undergoing implantation of a travoprost implant (iDose TR®; Glaukos) and either trabecular micro-bypass stent (iStent infinite®; Glaukos) implant or canaloplasty with or without cataract surgery in eyes with open-angle glaucoma (OAG).
METHODS: Adults undergoing the procedures of interest with ≥ 3 months of postoperative follow-up were included. The primary outcomes were changes in mean IOP and topical medication use from baseline to 3 months postoperatively. Analyses were conducted in the overall cohort and stratified by surgical context (with and without concurrent cataract surgery) and minimally invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS) modality (iStent infinite and canaloplasty), resulting in four subgroups: iDose TR + iStent infinite with phacoemulsification, iDose TR + iStent infinite, iDose TR + canaloplasty with phacoemulsification, and iDose TR + canaloplasty.

metas.titre: Development, validation, and cost-effectiveness analysis of an AI-assisted three-tiered glaucoma screening model in a community-based setting: protocol for a cluster randomized controlled trial.
metas.texte:
Development, validation, and cost-effectiveness analysis of an AI-assisted three-tiered glaucoma screening model in a community-based setting: protocol for a cluster randomized controlled trial.. INTRODUCTION: Glaucoma is the leading irreversible blinding eye disease worldwide and the global prevalence of glaucoma for individuals aged 40-80 years is estimated as 3.54%. Early screening and prevention wherever possible are essential interventions of chronic disease management for glaucoma, but there is currently a lack of a recognized glaucoma screening model for Chinese population. Therefore, this study intends to construct and validate an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted three-tiered glaucoma screening model based on the community population and assess its cost-effectiveness.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This is a community population-based cluster randomized controlled trial with a minimum of 6-year follow-up. metas.titre: Efficacy and safety of sepetaprost in patients with primary open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension: results from the randomised, phase 3 ANGEL-J1 study.
metas.texte:
Efficacy and safety of sepetaprost in patients with primary open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension: results from the randomised, phase 3 ANGEL-J1 study.. PURPOSE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of sepetaprost, a novel dual FP/EP3 receptor agonist, in patients with primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) or ocular hypertension (OHT).
STUDY DESIGN: ANGEL-J1 (NCT05495061) was a phase 3, randomised, investigator-masked, active-controlled, parallel-group, non-inferiority study across 49 sites in Japan.
METHODS: Adults with POAG or OHT were randomised 1:1 to topical sepetaprost 0.002% or latanoprost 0.005%, once daily for 3 months. The primary endpoint was change in mean diurnal intraocular pressure (IOP) from baseline at week 4 (non-inferiority margin, 1.5 mmHg); a key secondary endpoint was mean change in IOP from baseline over 3 months. Safety outcomes included the incidence of adverse drug reactions (ADRs).
RESULTS: In total, 325 patients were randomised to sepetaprost (n=162) or latanoprost (n=163). In mixed model for repeated measures analyses, ANGEL-J1 met its primary endpoint; the least-squares mean (± standard error) change in mean diurnal IOP from baseline at week 4 was -5.

metas.titre: Pascal selective laser trabeculoplasty (PSLT) in the treatment of ocular hypertension and open-angle glaucoma compared to travoprost eye drops: A non-inferiority clinical trial.
metas.texte:
Pascal selective laser trabeculoplasty (PSLT) in the treatment of ocular hypertension and open-angle glaucoma compared to travoprost eye drops: A non-inferiority clinical trial.. AIMS: To compare the effectiveness of PSLT and the use of topical prostaglandin eye drops in the treatment of ocular hypertensive (OHT) or open-angle glaucoma patients (POAG) in reducing intraocular pressure (IOP) and peak IOP.
METHODS: This is a non-inferiority randomized clinical trial, after washout, both patients eyes were randomized, one eye treated with PSLT (intervention group) and the contralateral eye treated with travoprost eye drops (controls). IOP, peak IOP by water drinking test (WDT), visual field (VF) and OCT were performed at baseline and at 7 days, 2, 6, 9 and 12 months after treatment. The primary outcome measure was to assess if the impact of PSLT on IOP and peak IOP is not inferior to that of the standard treatment (travoprost eye drops) by a margin not greater than the predefined threshold of 1.5 mmHg.
RESULTS: A total of 30 patients participated in this trial. The mean baseline IOP was similar in both groups, 18.8 ± 4.0 mmHg and 18.8 ± 4.2 mmHg, intervention and control respectively.

metas.titre: Neuroprotective Effect of Subconjunctival Melatonin Injections in 6-Hydroxydopamine-Induced Neurotoxic Eye Damage.
metas.texte: Neuroprotective Effect of Subconjunctival Melatonin Injections in 6-Hydroxydopamine-Induced Neurotoxic Eye Damage.. The search for new effective methods of neuroprotection is relevant for the treatment of a wide range of common eye diseases such as age-related macular degeneration, glaucoma, and diabetic retinopathy. Using a rabbit model of neurotoxic eye damage induced by intravitreal injection of the dopaminergic neurotoxin 6-hydroxydopamine (6-OHDA), we studied the effect of subconjunctival injections of 0.1% melatonin solution on pathophysiological and biochemical processes in the eye. Administration of 6-OHDA caused destruction of the retinal pigment epithelium, narrowing of retinal vessels, hemorrhages, decrease in ocular blood flow, and intraocular pressure, as well as reduced activity of α2-macroglobulin and concentrations of matrix metalloproteinase-9 and angiotensin-converting enzyme in the aqueous humor, vitreous body, and retina. metas.titre: Endophthalmitis following glaucoma drainage device surgery.
metas.texte:
Endophthalmitis following glaucoma drainage device surgery.. BACKGROUND: To evaluate the risk of endophthalmitis in glaucoma patients undergoing glaucoma drainage device (GDD) surgery.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study identified glaucoma patients utilising TriNetX's database who underwent GDD between 2004 and 2024 without a prior history of glaucoma surgery. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis estimated the cumulative incidence of endophthalmitis and a Cox proportional hazards model, adjusted for demographic and clinical covariates, was used to calculate adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) and confidence intervals (CIs) comparing outcomes between patients who underwent tube shunt surgery versus trabeculectomy. A scleral buckle (SB) cohort was added as a second comparator to GDD to contextualise infection risk related to hardware without bleb formation.
RESULTS: The GDD cohort included 12,849 patients (mean age 62.7 ± 19 years), compared with 9,006 trabeculectomy patients (67.9 ± 14.1) and 3,097 SB patients (45.1 ± 18.7). metas.titre: Post-LASIK Interface Fluid Syndrome: Evidence Synthesis and First Cases After Descemet Stripping Only (DSO).
metas.texte:
Post-LASIK Interface Fluid Syndrome: Evidence Synthesis and First Cases After Descemet Stripping Only (DSO).. PURPOSE: To review the mechanisms, clinical spectrum, and management of Interface Fluid Syndrome (IFS) after LASIK and to report a novel form of presentation developing after Descemet Stripping Only (DSO) for Fuchs endothelial dystrophy (FED) in post-LASIK eyes.
METHODS: This review included 83 studies, comprising clinical data from 225 previously reported eyes. Extracted variables included etiology (ocular hypertension, endothelial dysfunction, or other causes), diagnostic findings, management strategies, and clinical outcomes. Additionally, we report two novel cases of IFS after DSO, a setting that has not been previously described.
RESULTS: Among previously published cases, most (81.33%) were purely pressure-dependent, whereas 12% were primarily associated with endothelial dysfunction, and others reflected mixed or alternative mechanisms. Onset ranged from days to 31 years after LASIK. Acute findings typically included increased corneal thickness, reduced visual acuity, and falsely low central IOP measurements. metas.titre: Mannitol plus pilocarpine for primary acute angle-closure glaucoma: efficacy and safety analysis.
metas.texte:
Mannitol plus pilocarpine for primary acute angle-closure glaucoma: efficacy and safety analysis.. OBJECTIVE: To retrospectively analyze the efficacy and safety of mannitol (MAN) combined with pilocarpine (PC) in patients with primary acute angle-closure glaucoma (PAACG).
METHODS: A total of 103 PAACG patients were retrospectively enrolled and assigned to either the control group (PC alone) or the research group (MAN + PC). Treatment response, safety profiles, intraocular pressure (IOP), visual acuity (VA), hemodynamic parameters (end diastolic velocity [EDV], peak systolic velocity [PSV], and resistance index [RI]), anxiety/depression, and quality of life (Short-Form 36-Item Health Survey [SF-36]) were compared between the two groups. Furthermore, factors potentially associated with therapeutic efficacy and safety were analyzed.
RESULTS: The overall response rate was significantly higher in the research group than in the control group, whereas the incidence of adverse events were comparable between the two groups. metas.titre: Tau abnormalities and microglial remodeling in glaucoma: potential links to phagocytosis-related injury.
metas.texte:
Tau abnormalities and microglial remodeling in glaucoma: potential links to phagocytosis-related injury.. BACKGROUND: Glaucoma is a progressive optic neuropathy characterized by retinal ganglion cell degeneration and optic nerve damage. Increasing evidence indicates that glaucomatous injury is not limited to the retina, but may also involve downstream visual structures and neuroimmune responses. Tau abnormalities and microglial remodeling have each been reported in glaucoma models and human glaucomatous tissues, yet they are usually discussed as separate pathological findings. Whether these processes are connected, and how they might contribute to synaptic, dendritic, and axonal injury, remains insufficiently defined.
REVIEW FOCUS: This review examines current evidence for tau dysregulation and glaucoma-associated microglial remodeling in glaucoma. Experimental studies support retinal tau accumulation, altered phosphorylation, and redistribution from axonal to somatodendritic compartments after intraocular pressure elevation, whereas evidence for oligomeric tau remains limited to a single rat ocular-hypertension study. metas.titre: Association of serum TIM-3 and Galectin-9 levels with glaucoma progression: implications for clinical monitoring.
metas.texte:
Association of serum TIM-3 and Galectin-9 levels with glaucoma progression: implications for clinical monitoring.. BACKGROUND: Primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) causes irreversible blindness via retinal ganglion cell loss. Neuroinflammation and immune dysfunction drive its progression, yet the role of the TIM-3/Galectin-9 axis remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association of serum soluble TIM-3 (sTIM-3) and Galectin-9 levels with the progression of primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG).
METHODS: This retrospective analysis enrolled POAG patients from our ophthalmology department (January 2022-December 2024). After a minimum 12-month follow-up, participants were categorized as progression or stable based on visual field and optical coherence tomography (OCT) assessments. Healthy controls were age/sex-matched. Recorded clinical variables included IOP, CCT, visual fields, and OCT measures. Baseline concentrations of sTIM-3 and Galectin-9 in serum were determined by ELISA. Multivariate logistic regression assessed independent links between these markers and disease progression, supplemented by trend tests, E-value calculations, and subgroup analyses.

metas.titre: Advances in tumor necrosis factor-α inhibitors for the treatment of juvenile idiopathic arthritis-associated uveitis.
metas.texte: Advances in tumor necrosis factor-α inhibitors for the treatment of juvenile idiopathic arthritis-associated uveitis.. Juvenile idiopathic arthritis-associated uveitis (JIA-U) is a common and sight-threatening extra-articular manifestation of juvenile idiopathic arthritis, typically presenting as chronic noninfectious anterior uveitis. Its early symptoms are often insidious, and delayed detection and treatment may lead to cataract, glaucoma, macular edema, and irreversible visual impairment. Conventional treatment is based on glucocorticoids and immunosuppressants; however, some children continue to experience inadequate efficacy, glucocorticoid dependence, drug intolerance, or adverse events. In recent years, substantial progress has been made in the use of biologics for JIA-U. Among them, tumor necrosis factor-α inhibitors, particularly adalimumab, have shown potential for controlling ocular inflammation, reducing glucocorticoid exposure, and improving visual outcomes, thereby offering a new therapeutic avenue for patients with JIA-U. metas.titre: Deep Stromal Honeybee Sting Injury Causing Toxic Keratouveitis, Secondary Ocular Hypertension, and Iris Atrophy With Excellent Visual Recovery: A Case Report.
metas.texte: Deep Stromal Honeybee Sting Injury Causing Toxic Keratouveitis, Secondary Ocular Hypertension, and Iris Atrophy With Excellent Visual Recovery: A Case Report.. Honeybee sting injuries involving the cornea are uncommon but can result in severe visual morbidity because of mechanical injury and venom-induced toxicity. A 29-year-old man presented with severe pain, redness, watering, and profound visual loss in the right eye following accidental entry of a honeybee while driving. Visual acuity was perception of light with accurate projection of rays in all four quadrants. Slit-lamp examination revealed marked corneal edema, Descemet membrane folds, and a deep stromal foreign body in the superotemporal cornea. Intraocular pressure was elevated to 42 mmHg. Urgent foreign body removal and corneal scraping were performed, followed by intensive medical management including topical antibiotics, cycloplegics, antiglaucoma therapy, and systemic medications. Serial follow-up demonstrated progressive resolution of corneal edema and inflammation. metas.titre: Exosomes in Ophthalmology: Bridging Physiological Barriers for Precision Ocular Drug Delivery.
metas.texte:
Exosomes in Ophthalmology: Bridging Physiological Barriers for Precision Ocular Drug Delivery.. INTRODUCTION: Eye disorders such as age-related macular degeneration, diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, and uveitis persist as prominent contributors to visual impairment on a global scale. Conventional ocular drug delivery systems face a range of physiological hurdles, including tear film clearance, epithelium absorption, conjunctival absorption, and the formidable blood-retinal barrier. These challenges culminate in suboptimal ocular bioavailability, frequently compelling healthcare providers to resort to invasive drug administration methods.
METHODS: This review systematically evaluates recent literature focusing on exosome-based ocular drug delivery systems. Published preclinical and clinical studies were identified through structured searches of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science using the keywords "exosomes", "extracellular vesicles", "ocular drug delivery", "retina", and "ophthalmology". While selective laser trabeculoplasty (SLT) is a standard first-line therapy, its contact-based approach requires gonioscopy, which demands specialized skills and introduces minor corneal risks. Direct selective laser trabeculoplasty (DSLT) has emerged as an automated, non-contact evolution.MethodsA comprehensive search across five databases was conducted up to March 2026 for randomized controlled trials and non-randomized studies. Primary outcomes were mean absolute IOP reduction and treatment success (>20% IOP reduction). Secondary outcomes included reductions in medication burden and adverse events. metas.titre: Glaucoma in hospitalized older adults: polypharmacy, multimorbidity, and therapy discontinuation - a REPOSI registry analysis.
metas.texte:
Glaucoma in hospitalized older adults: polypharmacy, multimorbidity, and therapy discontinuation - a REPOSI registry analysis.. PURPOSE: To characterize the clinical profile, multimorbidity burden, medication use, reconciliation patterns, and outcomes of older patients with anamnestically recorded glaucoma or use of anti-glaucoma medications admitted to internal medicine and geriatric wards.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Prospective observational cohort study of 9,443 patients aged ≥ 65 years enrolled in the REPOSI registry (2008-2017) across 107 Italian hospitals. Patients with anamnestically recorded glaucoma (I = 346, 3.7%) were identified via ICD-9 code 365 or anti-glaucoma medications (ATC S01E). Baseline characteristics, comorbidity, medications, reconciliation, functional status, renal function, and outcomes were compared. Multivariable logistic regression assessed independent associations.

metas.texte:
Incidence of De Novo Glaucoma and Ocular Hypertension After DMEK vs DSAEK: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.. TOPIC: Post-keratoplasty glaucoma complicates endothelial keratoplasty, but its incidence with modern techniques remains uncertain. We conducted a systematic review estimating the pooled incidence of de novo glaucoma and ocular hypertension (OHT) in glaucoma-naïve adult eyes undergoing Descemet membrane endothelial keratoplasty (DMEK) or Descemet stripping automated endothelial keratoplasty (DSAEK).
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Post-keratoplasty glaucoma threatens optic nerve function and graft survival and may require therapy or surgery. Surgeons lack procedure-specific estimates to guide procedure selection and postoperative surveillance.
METHODS: We searched Embase, MEDLINE, Cochrane CENTRAL, CINAHL, Web of Science, Scopus, and ProQuest from inception to June 2025. Eligible studies enrolled adult eyes without pre-existing glaucoma undergoing DMEK or DSAEK and reported postoperative de novo glaucoma and/or OHT. metas.texte:
Cardiorespiratory fitness, cardiovascular risk, and disease-related outcomes in primary open-angle glaucoma: a cross-sectional study.. OBJECTIVE: To investigate the associations of objectively measured cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) with glaucoma-related functional, structural, and patient-reported outcomes and to compare its explanatory contribution with cumulative cardiovascular (CV) risk in patients with primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG).
DESIGN: Cross-sectional baseline analysis of the multicenter HIT-GLAUCOMA trial (NCT06058598).
SUBJECTS: One hundred ten patients with mild-to-moderate POAG.
METHODS: CRF was assessed by symptom-limited cardiopulmonary exercise testing and expressed as peak oxygen uptake (VO2peak). Cumulative CV risk was estimated using the Systematic COronary Risk Evaluation 2 (SCORE2). Missing data were addressed using multiple imputation. Multivariable linear regression models with restricted cubic splines were used to evaluate associations. Relative explanatory contributions of CRF and SCORE2 were explored using adequacy indices derived from model R2 values.

metas.texte:
Effect of delisting routine eye exams on optometric glaucoma diagnosis billings in Ontario.. OBJECTIVE: Routine eye examinations (REEs) are critical for glaucoma detection. In 2004, Ontario discontinued coverage for REEs for healthy individuals aged 20-64. We assessed whether this "delisting" policy affected the rate of new glaucoma diagnoses identified through REE billings.
DESIGN: A population-level intervention study PARTICIPANTS: Ontarians aged 20+ insured under Ontario's universal health coverage.
METHODS: Using Ontario health administrative data and segmented regression analysis, we assessed changes in the rate (per 10,000 population) of new glaucoma diagnoses billed by optometrists during REEs before (1998-2004) and after (2005-2019) coverage delisting individuals aged 20-64. A comparison group of seniors unaffected by the policy were also assessed across the same 2 periods.

metas.texte:
SS31 protects damaged retinal cells through the AMPK/DRP1 signaling pathway.. PURPOSE: Glaucoma is a group of neurodegenerative diseases characterized by progressive loss of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and optic nerve fibers. Mitochondrial dynamics contribute to the maintenance of neuronal homeostasis, and abnormalities can lead to the development of glaucoma. SS31 is a mitochondria-targeting short peptide that has been found to protect mitochondrial function and thereby protect damaged retina-associated cells. The aim of this study is to investigate whether SS31 protects damaged retinal cells by activating the AMPK/DRP1 pathway.
METHODS: The relationship between SS31 and oxidative stress was determined by live-cell imaging. metas.texte:
Case Report: Acute angle-closure glaucoma as the initial presentation of autosomal recessive bestrophinopathy caused by compound heterozygous BEST1 mutations.. BACKGROUND: Autosomal recessive bestrophinopathy (ARB) arises from compound heterozygous BEST1 mutations. Beyond retinal pathology, it may be associated with short axial length, shallow anterior chamber, and refractory angle-closure glaucoma (ACG). Filtration surgery carries a high recurrence rate and may yield suboptimal outcomes in selected BEST1-associated eyes, with the optimal surgical strategy remaining undefined.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 29-year-old female presented with refractory angle-closure glaucoma. Clinical examination revealed bilateral elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) and shallow anterior chambers. Retinal imaging demonstrated macular clefting and subretinal fluid. Ocular history was notable for repeated trabeculectomies, which provided transient IOP control. metas.titre: Optimizing Ocular Surface Disease (OSD) Management in Patients with Glaucoma: Expert Strategies from Asia.
metas.texte:
Optimizing Ocular Surface Disease (OSD) Management in Patients with Glaucoma: Expert Strategies from Asia.. INTRODUCTION: Ocular surface disease (OSD) commonly affects glaucoma patients and can occur due to the disease itself and multiple contributing factors, such as the long-term use of preserved topical medications, thereby impacting adherence and treatment outcomes. In Asia, rising glaucoma burden and variability in regional guidelines underscore the need for a practical synthesis of current literature in the region. This review summarizes the OSD treatment landscape in Asia and proposes a pragmatic approach for identifying and managing concomitant OSD in patients with glaucoma.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: Eight glaucoma specialists and a cornea expert representing eight Asian countries convened on 8th March 2025 at an industry‑sponsored expert meeting to discuss the current treatment landscape of concomitant OSD in glaucoma. A practical approach for identifying and managing concomitant OSD in glaucoma patients in daily clinics was subsequently developed based on published literature and expert input.

Extracellular purinergic signaling, mediated by nucleotides such as adenosine triphosphate (ATP) and adenosine, is a critical regulator of retinal homeostasis. Within the retina, this signaling pathway is indispensable for maintaining physiological functions. Dysregulation of extracellular purine balance is a key driver of retinal pathophysiology, contributing to inflammation, pathological angiogenesis, and neurodegeneration in diseases like diabetic retinopathy (DR), age-related macular degeneration (AMD), glaucoma, and retinopathy of prematurity (ROP). The hydrolysis of extracellular ATP to adenosine, primarily orchestrated by the sequential actions of NTPDase1/ENTPD1 (CD39) and ecto-5'-nucleotidase/NT5E (CD73), represents a fundamental mechanism for calibrating purinergic signals and shifting the microenvironment from pro-inflammatory to anti-inflammatory and protective. metas.titre: Rethinking delayed presentation in ophthalmology: A narrative review of biological and clinical consequences in resource-limited settings.
metas.texte: Rethinking delayed presentation in ophthalmology: A narrative review of biological and clinical consequences in resource-limited settings.. Delayed presentation remains a major contributor to visual impairment and blindness across diverse ophthalmic diseases, particularly in resource-limited settings where barriers to timely eye care remain substantial. Although advanced disease at presentation is widely recognized clinically, the broader biologic, neurodegenerative, developmental, surgical, and health systems consequences of delayed ophthalmic care have received comparatively less integrated attention. We examine delayed ophthalmic presentation as a multidimensional process that may influence inflammatory activity, ischemic injury, fibrosis, neurodegeneration, tissue remodeling, therapeutic responsiveness, and long-term visual outcomes across ophthalmic subspecialties. We further evaluate the clinical implications of delayed presentation in glaucoma, cataract, retinal disease, microbial keratitis, ocular trauma, pediatric ophthalmology, and ocular oncology, while examining the socioeconomic, geographic, behavioral, and health system determinants that contribute to delayed care. SUBJECTS/METHODS: We searched Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane Library from inception to November 2025 for studies reporting unexplained vision loss after SO removal following vitreoretinal surgery. Paired independent reviewers conducted screening, data extraction, and risk of bias assessment using the ROBINS-I tool. The pooled incidence was calculated using a random-effects meta-analysis.

metas.titre: Abiotrophia defectiva Endophthalmitis Associated With Exposed XEN Gel Stent.
metas.texte: Abiotrophia defectiva Endophthalmitis Associated With Exposed XEN Gel Stent.. An 80-year-old woman presented with a painful red eye four months after XEN gel stent implantation for primary open-angle glaucoma. Examination revealed an exposed gel stent through a conjunctival defect, corneal edema, hypopyon, and vitreous membranes, consistent with acute exogenous endophthalmitis. She underwent vitreous aspiration with intravitreal vancomycin and ceftazidime, followed by pars plana vitrectomy with stent explantation and silicone oil tamponade. Vitreous cultures grew Abiotrophia defectiva, recovered on routine media and identified to species by automated phenotypic testing within 6 hours, without molecular confirmation. Following silicone oil removal, vision returned to her baseline of 5/200, limited by prior central retinal vein occlusion. This represents the second reported case of A. defectiva endophthalmitis associated with an exposed gel stent. Contemporary automated identification may reduce diagnostic delay for this organism, though isolate-level susceptibility testing remains essential to guide targeted therapy.

Neurodegenerative diseases are increasingly recognized to involve detrimental interactions between the immune and nervous systems, yet whether failure of peripheral immune tolerance actively drives neuronal loss frequently remains unclear. metas.texte: Goniotomy as a safe and effective option for glaucoma secondary to typical ocular coloboma: A 12-month follow-up case.. A woman in her mid-50s presented with lifelong poor vision and progressive, painless bilateral visual deterioration. Clinical evaluation revealed markedly reduced visual acuity, elevated intraocular pressure, bilateral inferior iris coloboma, zonular laxity, nuclear cataracts, partially closed angles and hypoplastic trabecular meshwork. Sequential phacoemulsification with intraocular lens implantation combined with a 120° goniotomy was performed in both eyes. Intraoperatively, residual embryonic tissue overlying the trabecular meshwork and a diminished red reflex were observed. Postoperatively, the patient experienced rapid improvement in visual acuity and intraocular pressure, with restoration of corneal clarity and wide opening of the anterior chamber angles within 1 week. Fundus examination subsequently revealed an inferonasal choroidal coloboma with retinal vessels traversing the defect. At 1-year, visual acuity remained significantly improved and intraocular pressure was stable without medication, with no complications such as hypotony or retinal detachment.

The assay is constructed using a target-triggered cascaded strand-displacement circuit that enforces sequential molecular recognition prior to amplification, thereby improving specificity. Upon target recognition, rolling circle amplification (RCA) generates DNA products that simultaneously produce a thioflavin T (ThT) fluorescence signal via G-quadruplex (G4) formation and sequester the Cas12a/gRNA Activator strand to suppress ROX fluorescence. Perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) pose health risks, but their association with glaucoma, cataracts, and age-related macular degeneration remains uncertain. First, a cross-sectional analysis of NHANES (2005-2008) was performed using multiple logistic regression and mixture models, including weighted quantile sum (WQS), quantile g-computation (QGC), and Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR), to examine single and mixed PFAS exposures in relation to ocular diseases. Second, Mendelian randomization was applied to further explore the PFOS-glaucoma association. Third, network toxicology and in vitro experiments were employed to generate mechanistic hypotheses. Cross-sectional results suggested positive associations between PFOS and glaucoma, and between PFNA and cataracts. Glaucoma is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disease, and the dysfunction of the neurovascular unit (NVU) in optic nerve head (ONH) has been gradually recognized to contribute to the neurodegeneration progression, yet its heterogeneity features remain poorly understood. Here, we established rat models of high intraocular pressure (HIOP) and lipopolysaccharide-induced ocular inflammation (LPS), and performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of ONH-centered tissues to characterize the cellular and molecular characteristics of NVU and its main cell components. Distinct alterations in the cellular composition and intercellular communication of the ONH-NVU were observed among Ctrl, HIOP and LPS conditions. metas.texte: Bilateral Keratouveitis and Secondary Glaucoma in a Young Dog With Immune-Mediated Polyarthritis and Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome.. A 7-month-old intact female mixed-breed dog presented emergently for inability to walk, lethargy, and vomiting. The patient was diagnosed with immune-mediated polyarthritis (IMPA) and secondary systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS). Bilateral keratouveitis and secondary glaucoma developed within 24 h of presentation. Thorough diagnostic testing failed to identify an underlying etiology. Despite aggressive medical management, the patient developed rapid vision loss. Due to poor visual prognosis and anticipated need for long-term medical management, both eyes were enucleated. Histopathological evaluation of both globes revealed severe corneal endothelial injury most consistent with endotheliitis with associated uveitis and endophthalmitis. One patient demonstrated scleral melt and conjunctival thinning beneath the large PGI plate. Both patients received maximum doses of systemic corticosteroids and mycophenolate mofetil to control ocular inflammation. Owing to the high risk of infection and re-exposure, each patient underwent PGI explantation. DESIGN: Retrospective, single-center cohort study.
METHODS: Eyes undergoing small-incision SSF or ISHF between 2019 and 2024 were identified. Demographics, surgical indications, IOL types, refractive accuracy, and postoperative complications were analyzed. Refractive outcomes were evaluated using spherical equivalent refractive accuracy (SERA) and absolute SERA (ASERA).
RESULTS: 132 eyes from 125 adult patients were included. 56 eyes underwent SSF, and 76 underwent ISHF. Indications included subluxated IOL (58%), dislocated IOL (17%), aphakia (20%), and uveitis-glaucoma-hyphema syndrome (5%). In the SSF group, MX60E or ET IOLs predominated, while CT Lucia 602 was most common in ISHF. PURPOSE: Obesity is a serious health problem worldwide and is associated with several ocular conditions, including glaucoma, cataract, and age-related macular degeneration. Elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) is a well-established and modifiable risk factor for glaucomatous optic neuropathy. This study aimed to evaluate early changes in IOP following laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy and to examine their relationship with weight loss. A secondary exploratory aim was to describe whether postoperative improvement in hypertension or diabetes mellitus was accompanied by additional changes in IOP.

metas.titre: Conclusions and Therapeutic Implications of AA.
metas.texte: Conclusions and Therapeutic Implications of AA.. AA is essential for several tissues in the body, as they are involved in many physiological and pathological processes. Its regulatory role in inflammation, immune response regulation, cell cycle, and membrane structural organization and its ability to control the expression and function(s) of several receptors and convey messages to and from the nucleus are of particular significance. Fine-tuning the metabolism of AA may lead to the development of prevention and management strategies for several diseases, including but not limited to sepsis, inflammatory bowel disease, diabetes mellitus, cancer, coronary heart disease, atherosclerosis, MASLD (NAFLD), hypertension, metabolic syndrome, uveitis, glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, glomerulonephritis, ischemia-reperfusion injury, lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, and drug-resistant infections and cancer. AA is needed for normal brain growth and development, pregnancy, regeneration of the liver and heart, and hematopoiesis. AA can be administered orally, parenterally as needed, and as lipid nanoparticles to target specific tissues.

metas.titre: 1,3,4-Oxadiazole-sulfonamide hybrids: recent advances in biological activities, structure-activity relationships, and therapeutic applications.
metas.texte: 1,3,4-Oxadiazole-sulfonamide hybrids: recent advances in biological activities, structure-activity relationships, and therapeutic applications.. Molecular hybridization has emerged as an effective strategy in medicinal chemistry for the development of multifunctional therapeutic agents with improved biological performance. Among the various hybrid scaffolds investigated, 1,3,4-oxadiazole-sulfonamide hybrids have gained considerable attention owing to the complementary pharmacological properties of both pharmacophores. The integration of the 1,3,4-oxadiazole nucleus and sulfonamide moiety within a single molecular framework has generated structurally diverse compounds exhibiting promising activities against a broad range of biological targets. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the biological activities and structure-activity relationships (SARs) of 1,3,4-oxadiazole-sulfonamide hybrids reported over the past two decades. metas.texte: Rodent models of glaucoma: Pathogenic mechanisms, phenotyping strategies, and translational relevance.. Glaucoma comprises a heterogeneous group of optic neuropathies characterized by progressive degeneration of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and their axons. Rodent models have been widely used to investigate disease mechanisms, identify neuroprotective targets and evaluate emerging therapeutic strategies because they are cost-effective, genetically tractable and experimentally controllable. However, mice and rats differ substantially from humans in anterior-segment anatomy, trabecular meshwork architecture, Schlemm's canal development, lamina cribrosa structure, RGC composition and optic nerve head vascular supply. These interspecies differences influence model construction, phenotypic interpretation and the translational value of preclinical findings. metas.texte: Shear Stress and Pressure Homeostasis in the Eye's Aqueous Outflow Pathway.. Glaucoma is the most common cause of irreversible blindness. Many patients with glaucoma suffer from elevated intraocular pressure (IOP), due to impaired drainage of aqueous humor fluid from the eye, and all current treatments are designed to lower IOP, implicating dysregulation of IOP as an important clinical problem. Because IOP is maintained within a narrow range over a lifetime in a healthy eye, it is thought that mechanically driven feedback loops within the eye maintain IOP homeostasis, and in fact, good evidence for such loops now exists. Here we revisit the fluid mechanics of aqueous humor flow in the eye to estimate fluid shear stresses in relevant aqueous drainage tissues, in order to identify mechanical signals that may be involved in IOP homeostatic feedback loops. We find that shear stresses within the juxtacanalicular tissue are likely too small to play a significant role, except perhaps in the very immediate vicinity of the inner wall of Schlemm's canal. metas.titre: The Emerging Role of Cellular Mechanical Memory in Aqueous Humor Outflow Dysfunction in Glaucoma.
metas.texte: The Emerging Role of Cellular Mechanical Memory in Aqueous Humor Outflow Dysfunction in Glaucoma.. Emerging evidence suggests that cells can retain information about previous mechanical environments and subsequently exhibit altered phenotypes even after the original mechanical stimulus is removed. This phenomenon is known as cellular mechanical memory that occurs in three phases: memory acquisition, storage, and recall. The literature supports a model in which mechanical experiences become encoded through interconnected cytoskeletal, nuclear, metabolic, and epigenetic mechanisms. Mechanical memory is increasingly recognized as a central regulator of cell fate and tissue remodeling, as well as a fundamental principle in development, aging, fibrosis, cancer, and regenerative medicine. We here give a concise overview of the historical origins and defining features of mechanical memory, discuss the emergence of mechanical memory in aqueous humor outflow dysfunction in glaucoma, summarize key unanswered questions, and close with a discussion of the clinical relevance of targeting mechanical memory for therapeutic purposes.

INTRODUCTION: Non-infectious uveitis (NIU) is a chronic immune-mediated ocular inflammatory disease that may cause irreversible visual impairment. This systematic review and network meta-analysis evaluated systemic immunosuppressive therapies for NIU.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception to May 2, 2026. Randomized controlled trials and prospective comparative cohort studies evaluating systemic immunomodulatory or biologic therapies for NIU were included. The primary efficacy outcome was treatment failure. Tacrolimus, a macrolide calcineurin inhibitor, has emerged as a steroid-sparing alternative for T-cell-mediated ocular disease. This review summarizes the mechanism of action, ocular pharmacology, clinical applications, and safety profile of topical tacrolimus.

metas.titre: Breaking the Rules: Museum Data Reveal Divergent Support for Classic Ecogeographical Rules in North American Flying Squirrels.
metas.texte: Breaking the Rules: Museum Data Reveal Divergent Support for Classic Ecogeographical Rules in North American Flying Squirrels.. Ecogeographic generalizations or "rules", such as Bergmann's rule and Allen's rule, propose that endotherms in colder climates evolve larger bodies and shorter appendages to minimize heat loss. These patterns are hypothesized to reflect physiological adaptations to thermal stress through reduced surface area-to-volume ratios. Although these rules have been extensively evaluated across birds and mammals, their applicability to arboreal gliders remains untested, with little consideration of how alternative ecological and evolutionary drivers may structure morphological variation in flying squirrels across environmental gradients. This pilot study evaluated the feasibility and immediate effects of a multimodal, dance-integrated educational video package designed to improve eye health knowledge, attitudes, and preventive intentions among Nigerian adults. Between April 11 and June 22, 2025, adults recruited through optometry clinics and community outreach programmes viewed culturally tailored educational videos addressing at least one eye condition (myopia, cataract, or glaucoma) and general eye health, including common myths and preventive practices. Pre-post changes were assessed using paired comparisons, with subgroup analyses by educational attainment. metas.texte:
The Second and Third Decade After 103Pd Plaque Brachytherapy for Choroidal Melanoma.. PURPOSE: To determine long-term visual and ocular outcomes in a large cohort of patients with choroidal melanoma treated using palladium-103 (103Pd) plaque brachytherapy.
DESIGN: This is a retrospective cohort study.
PARTICIPANTS: 170 patients with a minimum of 10 years of continuous follow-up at The New York Eye Cancer Center following 103Pd plaque brachytherapy treatment for choroidal melanoma.
METHODS: The study includes collected data consisting of patient demographic characteristics, tumor features, such as size, location, and AJCC clinical T-category (cT), visual outcomes, variables related to post-treatment retinopathy management, and long-term ocular comorbidities.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary endpoints were tumor control, ocular conservation, and visual acuity. We present a 6-year-old female with recurrent acute cellular rejection and steroid-induced glaucoma due to high-dose corticosteroid therapy. Consequently, AZA was incorporated into her calcineurin-inhibitor-based regimen to reduce steroid dose. metas.titre: Anterior Segment Ischemia and Neurotrophic Keratopathy Following Ultrasound Cycloplasty in Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma.
metas.texte: Anterior Segment Ischemia and Neurotrophic Keratopathy Following Ultrasound Cycloplasty in Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma.. Ultrasound cycloplasty (UCP) is a minimally invasive, non-incisional glaucoma procedure that has emerged in recent years and is generally associated with few complications. We report a case of a patient with acute angle-closure glaucoma underwent UCP for IOP control. She developed iris neovascularization and neurotrophic keratopathy（NK）at postoperative week 6, followed by hypopyon, flattening of the anterior chamber, and thinning of the peripheral cornea at postoperative week 11, 12, and 14, respectively. We concluded that UCP can lead to anterior segment ischemia (ASI) and NK, which manifest as iris neovascularization, painless corneal epithelial defects, peripheral corneal thinning, hypopyon, and flattening of the anterior chamber. Preoperative screening for high-risk factors is essential before performing UCP.

metas.texte: Advancing nanomaterials for treatment of eye diseases: a review.. Ocular diseases involving both the anterior and posterior segments-such as dry eye disease, keratitis, glaucoma, cataracts, diabetic retinopathy, retinal vein occlusion, and ocular tumors-remain major contributors to global visual impairment. Conventional topical and systemic therapies are limited by rapid clearance, restricted penetration across ocular barriers, and poor bioavailability, particularly for posterior-segment targets. Nanotechnology has introduced a transformative therapeutic paradigm by enabling controlled pharmacokinetics, enhanced tissue penetration, and site-specific delivery. A wide range of engineered nanomaterials-including polymeric nanoparticles, lipid-based carriers, dendrimers, metallic and metal-oxide nanoparticles, mesoporous silica systems, cerium oxide nanozymes, carbon quantum dots, nanogels, and electrospun nanofibers-has demonstrated improved drug loading, sustained release, ocular surface retention, and compatibility with biologics and gene-based agents. metas.texte: AKAP1 Protects Retinal Ganglion Cells and Preserves Vision by Improving Mitochondrial and Synaptic Health in Glaucomatous Neurodegeneration.. Glaucoma, a leading cause of irreversible blindness, is characterized by progressive loss of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and lacks effective neuroprotective therapies. Despite evidence implicating mitochondrial dysfunction in glaucoma, the mechanisms linking elevated intraocular pressure, synaptic dysfunction, mitochondrial failure, and RGC death remain incompletely understood. Here we identify the mitochondrial scaffold protein A-kinase anchoring protein 1 (AKAP1) as a critical regulator of RGC resilience in glaucoma. Progress in the Synthesis of Evidence in Glaucoma: What We Know and the Gaps that Remain.. PURPOSE: Glaucoma is one of the leading causes of blindness worldwide, necessitating evidence-informed interventions and strategies to improve the quality of life of affected individuals. In this review, we examined progress in evidence over the past decade and discussed its implications and the ways forward for delivery of glaucoma care globally, embedded within a rapid evidence and gap-mapping exercise of systematic reviews and/or meta-analyses published between 2015 and 2025.
METHODS: Using a predefined conceptual framework, ten domains were identified as relevant to evidence synthesis in glaucoma care. Within each domain, we assessed areas of strength and identified remaining evidence gaps. Findings were synthesised narratively and recommendations provided to inform future research priorities and advancement in glaucoma care.

Inflammatory and immune-mediated ocular diseases encompass a spectrum of conditions that arise from dysregulated immune-inflammatory responses marked by a chronic clinical course, a propensity for relapse, and a tendency to cause significant ocular tissue damage, which can lead to profound impairment of visual function. Dysregulation of the balance between immune cell subpopulations is central to the pathogenesis of many of these diseases. At present, non-specific treatments such as glucocorticoids and immunosuppressants form the cornerstone of therapy for inflammatory and immune-mediated ocular diseases. However, these treatments often suffer from poor bioavailability and targeting, cumbersome or invasive administration methods, and are associated with side effects such as increased intraocular pressure (IOP), cataracts, or glaucoma with frequent administration. ROS-related ophthalmic diseases span the ocular surface as well as the anterior and posterior segments of the eye. Dry eye disease (DED), glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy (DR) and age-related macular degeneration (AMD) have distinct anatomical targets but share common pathophysiological features, including oxidative stress, inflammation, vascular dysfunction, epithelial injury or neurodegeneration. Conventional ocular drug delivery and therapeutic modalities are hindered by severe limitations, including low bioavailability in the posterior segment of the eye and the requirement for frequent invasive administration. Nanozymes, an emerging class of therapeutic agents that integrate the properties of nanomaterials with natural enzyme-like catalytic activity, can efficiently scavenge excess reactive oxygen species (ROS) in focal lesions, modulate inflammatory factors, and remodel the pathological microenvironment, thereby providing a novel approach to the treatment of ROS-related ophthalmic diseases. metas.titre: A New Frontier: Partial Cellular Reprogramming in Plastic Surgery.
metas.texte: A New Frontier: Partial Cellular Reprogramming in Plastic Surgery.. Partial cellular reprogramming employs Yamanaka factors to shift aging cells toward a younger epigenetic state without compromising cellular identity. Over two decades, this Nobel Prize winning breakthrough has advanced from the bench to a first in-human trial in 2026 for optic neuropathy and glaucoma. Here, we outline the foundation of partial cellular reprogramming and delineate its intersection with our field. Defined by innovation, plastic surgery can shape how partial reprogramming is applied in what may prove to be a transformative chapter for our specialty.

metas.texte: Mastering the eye: Clinical paradigm shifts from optical restoration to genomic correction.. Historically, the main operation for cataract was couching, and the interior of the living eye could not be examined until Hermann von Helmholtz introduced the ophthalmoscope in 1851. Since the mid-twentieth century, seven advances have reshaped ophthalmic care. Harold Ridley implanted the first intraocular lens in 1949, and the ophthalmologist Charles Kelman and the engineer Anton Banko developed phacoemulsification, reported in 1967. Robert Machemer performed the first pars plana vitrectomy in 1970, while David Huang and colleagues described optical coherence tomography in 1991. Endothelial keratoplasty, developed by Gerrit Melles and others between 1998 and 2006, replaced only the failing corneal endothelium instead of the full thickness of the cornea. Anti-VEGF therapy followed the purification of VEGF by Napoleone Ferrara and colleagues in 1989 and the approval of ranibizumab in 2006. metas.texte: Role of Chromatin-Associated RNAs in Eye Physiology and Pathology.. Noncoding RNAs, including long noncoding RNAs, enhancer RNAs, circular RNAs, and small nuclear and nucleolar RNAs, represent a major, yet still largely uncharacterized, regulatory layer in the eye. A subset of these molecules, chromatin-associated RNAs (caRNAs), physically interacts with DNA and nuclear protein complexes to influence genome organization, transcriptional output, and stress responses. Although caRNAs have emerged as essential regulators of chromatin topology and gene expression in diverse tissues, their identity, dynamics, and mechanisms in the retina and retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) remain elusive. Recent high-resolution genomic studies, disease transcriptomes, and mechanistic studies implicate dysregulated caRNAs in age-related macular degeneration, glaucoma, and diabetic retinopathy, yet causal chromatin-level functions have rarely been demonstrated. metas.texte: Research Progress on Intraocular Pressure-lowering Drugs, Commonly Used Clinical Adjuvants, and Emerging Neuroprotective Agents for Glaucomatous Optic Neuropathy.. Glaucomatous optic neuropathy (GON) is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide, characterized by progressive retinal ganglion cell (RGC) loss. Current clinical treatment relies primarily on IOP-lowering drugs, but a subset of patients continues to experience progressive optic nerve damage. Adjuvant therapies such as antioxidants and calcium channel blockers have limited efficacy. Emerging neuroprotective strategies including NMDA receptor antagonists, neurotrophic factors, and gene therapy remain in preclinical or early-stage trials. This review systematically summarizes the mechanisms, clinical applications, and limitations of these three drug categories, with emphasis on emerging neuroprotective agents, aiming to guide future research directions.

metas.titre: The rise of modern tonometry: the evolution of intraocular pressure measurement.
metas.texte:
The rise of modern tonometry: the evolution of intraocular pressure measurement.. INTRODUCTION: Intraocular pressure (IOP) is the primary biomarker for the diagnosis and management of glaucoma, a progressive optic neuropathy and the second leading cause of blindness worldwide. Its pathophysiology involves an imbalance between aqueous humor production and drainage that elevates IOP, ultimately damaging the optic nerve. IOP exhibits substantial circadian fluctuations, and single-point clinical measurements frequently fail to capture peak diurnal pressure, thereby underestimating the risk of disease progression, delaying necessary intervention, and obscuring patient compliance with pharmaceutical therapies.
AREAS COVERED: This review synthesizes historical, contemporary, and emerging IOP measurement technologies, examining their underlying physical principles, clinical utility, and limitations, with particular emphasis on their capacity to characterize the dynamic, time-varying nature of IOP. The search drew on Google Scholar and manufacturers' websites, focusing on physical principles and systems not yet FDA-approved or clinically tested.

metas.titre: Autophagy in ocular health and disease: From mechanistic insights to therapeutic perspectives.
metas.texte: Autophagy in ocular health and disease: From mechanistic insights to therapeutic perspectives.. Autophagy represents a lysosomal degradative pathway through which cells systematically break down and recycle their own constituents, including proteins, lipid droplets, and entire organelles, by sequestering them within double-membrane autophagosomes prior to lysosomal fusion. Beyond its role as a fundamental quality control mechanism, this process critically shapes cellular metabolism and preserves intracellular equilibrium. In ocular biology, autophagic activity is involved in structural morphogenesis during eye development and becomes dysregulated across a spectrum of vision-threatening disorders. This review synthesises current evidence on autophagy throughout distinct ocular compartments, with particular attention given to its pathogenic contributions to corneal disease, cataract formation, glaucomatous neurodegeneration, and major retinopathies, with the goal of advancing the understanding of the underlying mechanism in this evolving field.

metas.texte: Retinal neurodegeneration as accelerated ocular aging: a review of nutritional and metabolic supplements.. Retinal neurodegeneration is a major cause of irreversible vision loss and a shared feature of age-related macular degeneration (AMD), diabetic retinopathy (DR), and glaucoma (GL). Increasing evidence suggests that these conditions share important pathways with retinal aging, including mitochondrial dysfunction, metabolic insufficiency, redox imbalance, chronic low-grade inflammation, and progressive neuronal vulnerability. While antioxidant and micronutrient supplementation, most notably the Age-Related Eye Disease Study (AREDS) formulations, has demonstrated benefit in selected AMD populations, emerging metabolic and nutraceutical strategies targeting aging-related pathways are of unproven benefit. Posterior cortical atrophy (PCA) is a clinical syndrome characterized by progressive higher-order visual impairment and is most frequently associated with AD pathology, although other neurodegenerative causes may be possible. We assessed documented dry eye disease (DED) and its associations with active-ingredient burden, treatment duration, and preservative exposure. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 357 adults receiving topical antiglaucoma therapy at a tertiary center who had complete treatment and ocular-surface data. Ocular-surface testing was prompted by symptoms or clinical judgment. The first eligible visit identified during chronological record review was analyzed for each patient. DED was based on the treating ophthalmologist's documented diagnosis. Logistic regression evaluated treatment-related factors. Results: DED was documented in 171/357 patients within this selected sample (47.9%; 95% CI 42.8-53.1%). metas.texte: Biological Restoration of Conventional Aqueous Outflow Pathways in Glaucoma.. Glaucoma causes progressive damage to the optic nerve, and reducing intraocular pressure is the only clinically proven way to slow the disease. Although current medical, laser, and surgical treatments mainly change aqueous humor dynamics, they do not counteract the cellular and extracellular abnormalities of the conventional outflow pathway. Growing evidence shows that loss and dysfunction of trabecular meshwork cells impair aqueous humor drainage, supporting regenerative approaches that rebuild the outflow system rather than bypass it. In this narrative review, we present novel stem cell-based strategies to regenerate the trabecular meshwork and Schlemm's canal, particularly trabecular meshwork (TM) stem cells, mesenchymal stem cells, pluripotent stem cell-derived TM-like cells, and neural crest-derived progenitors. Nail-patella syndrome (NPS) is a rare autosomal dominant multisystem disorder characterized by a variable combination of nail abnormalities, patellar hypoplasia or dysplasia, elbow involvement, and iliac horns, with possible renal, ophthalmological, neurological, and skeletal manifestations. Recognition may be substantially delayed when individual abnormalities are assessed separately or attributed to age-related and degenerative musculoskeletal disease. We report the case of a 76-year-old woman evaluated for progressive bilateral knee pain, gait impairment, and chronic multisite musculoskeletal symptoms. Congenital thumbnail abnormalities and long-standing restriction of elbow extension had been present since childhood. Suspicion of NPS was first raised at the age of 43 years after bilateral iliac horns were identified radiographically in one of her grandsons. Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) is expanding eye care beyond image-based detection toward prognosis, treatment-response prediction, monitoring, triage, and clinician-facing decision support. We evaluated AI across eye-disease screening, diagnosis, prognosis, treatment response, and decision support, emphasizing validation, explainability, and clinical readiness. Methods: This PROSPERO-registered review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. Six databases plus supplementary routes identified English-language literature published from 1 January 2015 through 10 August 2026. Background/Objectives: We aimed to evaluate nonadherence to topical glaucoma therapy and identify risk factors for repeated prescription fulfillment failure in a large national population-based cohort. Methods: The electronic medical records from a large health maintenance organization were retrospectively reviewed for all patients aged 18 years or older with a diagnosis of glaucoma from 2000 to 2023. Data on patients who had purchased at least one anti-glaucoma medication were retrieved. Compliance was defined as prescription fulfillment within predefined expiration windows of 1, 2, and 3 months. Repeated nonadherence was defined as three unfulfilled prescriptions within a 3-month expiration window. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify risk factors for repeated failure. Results: Among 40,200 treated patients, ≥80% cumulative prescription fulfillment was achieved in 80.3% of the population under a 3-month expiration definition. Background/Objectives: Prostaglandin analogues may cause prostaglandin-associated periorbitopathy (PAP). We evaluated treatment patterns, persistence, and intraocular pressure (IOP) outcomes of OMDI in Korean patients with NTG. Methods: This retrospective study included 403 eyes of 218 patients with NTG who initiated OMDI and were followed for up to 12 months. Patients received monotherapy, adjunctive therapy, or switching therapy. IOP was analyzed using a three-level linear mixed-effects model, and persistence was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Results: OMDI was prescribed as monotherapy in 88 patients (40.4%), adjunctive therapy in 25 (11.5%), and switching therapy in 105 (48.2%). Among switchers, PAP was the most common reason (68.6%). Outcome parameters at 12 months were intraocular pressure (IOP), number of topical antiglaucoma medications, surgical success, complications, and reinterventions.

metas.titre: Delayed presentation of intraocular pentastomiasis resulting in unilateral blindness in a Congolese child.
metas.texte: Delayed presentation of intraocular pentastomiasis resulting in unilateral blindness in a Congolese child.. We report the case of a 6-year-old girl who presented with a motile larva in the anterior chamber of the right eye, associated with anterior uveitis, secondary glaucoma, and blindness. The larva was identified macroscopically as Armillifer grandis, a pentastomid parasite with snakes and other reptiles as definitive hosts. Intraocular pressure normalized and intraocular inflammation resolved within days following removal. This case is reported because ocular pentastomiasis is exceptionally rare compared with visceral pentastomiasis. It underscores the vision-threatening potential of intraocular pentastomiasis and the importance of early recognition and prompt surgical extraction to prevent visual impairment. Ocular pentastomiasis is a rare parasitic infection of the eye caused by larval stages of pentastomid arthropods, most commonly Armillifer and less frequently Linguatula species. metas.titre: Lens particle-induced pediatric glaucoma following congenital cataract surgery: a case report.
metas.texte: Lens particle-induced pediatric glaucoma following congenital cataract surgery: a case report.. A 13-year-old boy with a history of bilateral lens extraction for congenital cataract at 4 months of age presented with nausea and vomiting. Tafluprost had been administrated once daily to both eyes since the age of 7 years, and intraocular pressure (IOP) in both eyes remained around 20 mm Hg before this visit. On examination, IOP was 21 mm Hg in the right eye and 52 mm Hg in the left eye. The next day, the IOP in the left eye decreased to 10 mm Hg. No significant floaters were seen in the anterior chamber of either eye. Multiple lens fragments were present in the left angle. Four days later, the left eye IOP had increased to 60 mm Hg, and lens fragments were observed floating in the left anterior recess. Based on the course and findings, lens-induced glaucoma was considered the most reasonable cause for the elevated IOP; therefore, anterior chamber washout was performed. Eighteen months postoperatively, no fragments remained in the anterior chamber, and IOP remained 17-19 mm Hg. In this case, gonioscopy was useful in establishing the cause of IOP elevation.

Precise segmentation of the optic disc (OD) and optic cup (OC) enables accurate cup-to-disc ratio (CDR) calculation, which serves as an important reference for glaucoma evaluation. metas.titre: Buoyancy-Mediated in Situ Phase-Transition Microbubbles Enable Efficient Aqueous Humor Drug Delivery for Accelerated Corneal Endothelial Regeneration.

The corneal endothelium plays a pivotal role in maintaining corneal clarity, and its damage leads to a hydration dysfunction and secondary glaucoma. We previously identified XMU-MP-1, a Hippo pathway inhibitor, as a potent stimulator of corneal endothelial cell proliferation in nonhuman primate models. However, its therapeutic potential is limited by poor intraocular permeability and low bioavailability. Herein, we report an engineered perfluoropentane (PFP)-cored lipid microbubble (MB) platform for the buoyancy-mediated targeted delivery of XMU-MP-1. Post intracameral injection, drug-loaded microbubbles (D@MB) undergo spontaneous in situ liquid-to-gas phase transition at physiological temperature, which grants them buoyancy-driven upward movement in aqueous humor to maintain continuous direct contact with the endothelial layer, achieving an extended retention of over 72 h in the anterior chamber. metas.texte: Neuroprotectant development from small molecule inhibitors of CHOP/ATF4 expression.. Glaucoma is a neurodegenerative disease that is in urgent need of neuroprotective therapies. We previously revealed the critical role of neuronal endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress induced by optic nerve injury in glaucomatous neurodegeneration. We also demonstrated that modulation of the ATF4-CHOP branch of ER stress provides significant neuroprotection. Here, we present multiple new chemical series identified by high-throughput screening that inhibit ER stress-induced C/EBP homologous protein (CHOP) expression. We perform a structure-activity relationship analysis of one "hit" compound and establish two analogs with potent activities on inhibiting the expression of CHOP and activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4). We further demonstrate their neuroprotective efficacy in two optic neuropathy models; in both models, they increase survival of retinal ganglion cell somata and axons and preserve visual function. METHODS: Medicare Benefits Schedule (MBS) procedure claims and Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS)/Repatriation PBS dispensing data were analysed from 2015 to 2024. RESULTS: Between 2015 and 2024, 344,370 SLT procedures were recorded. Rates rose from 127 to 150 per 100,000 (β = 1,335 procedures/year; 95% CI 969-1,701; p < 0.001). Although initial therapy relies on corticosteroids, patients with chronic inflammation often require systemic immunomodulatory therapy (IMT) or local sustained-release steroids. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used the TriNetX Network to identify adults (ages ≥ 18 years) with chronic uveitis treated with systemic IMT or local corticosteroid therapy. metas.titre: Mishel theory-based perioperative nursing after trabeculectomy for primary glaucoma: effects on illness uncertainty, self-management, and quality of life.
metas.texte:
Mishel theory-based perioperative nursing after trabeculectomy for primary glaucoma: effects on illness uncertainty, self-management, and quality of life.. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effects of a perioperative nursing intervention based on Mishel's Uncertainty in Illness Theory in patients with primary glaucoma undergoing trabeculectomy.
METHODS: This single-center, two-arm, parallel-group randomized controlled study enrolled 198 patients undergoing first trabeculectomy at The First Affiliated Hospital of Suzhou University between February 2024 and December 2025. Participants were randomly allocated 1:1 to routine perioperative ophthalmic nursing or routine care plus a structured Mishel theory-based nursing intervention. Assessments were conducted 1 day before surgery (T0), at discharge (T1), and at 1 month (T2) and 3 months (T3) after surgery. The primary outcome was illness uncertainty measured using the Mishel Uncertainty in Illness Scale. Secondary outcomes included psychological status, discharge readiness, self-management, medication adherence, sleep quality, vision-related quality of life, satisfaction with nursing care, postoperative ophthalmic outcomes, and complications.

METHODS: A longitudinal assessment of blood pressure, intraocular pressure, retinal function, structure, and perfusion was conducted in spontaneously hypertensive rats and Wistar-Kyoto rats. Transcriptomic analyses and immunofluorescence staining were performed to investigate hypertension-associated retinal biochemical changes. AAV-mediated knockdown of endothelin 2 was used to investigate its mechanistic role.
RESULTS: Hypertensive rats develop accelerated retinal degeneration marked by retinal thinning, functional impairment, reduced perfusion, and progressive neuroinflammation. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study of deidentified, patient-initiated secure messages sent between June 2014 and July 2024. metas.texte: [The perimetry ant tonometry in real clinical practice of managing patients with glaucoma: facilities and possibilities].. The anonymous survey of 107 ophthalmologists was carried out to assess facilities and practical application of diagnostic equipment in detection and management of glaucoma patients. It is established that main load of dispensary monitoring lies upon out-patient sector (81.8% of interrogated physicians of this level). However, only 12.5% of them have dedicated hours for glaucoma patients as compared to 35.3% of in-patient physicians (p=0.03). This indicates at time deficiency for full-value management of glaucoma patients at the primary care level that may negatively affect quality of dispensary monitoring. Canine inherited ocular diseases exhibit significant genetic heterogeneity, mirroring many human ophthalmic conditions. This study conducted an extensive screening of 90 OMIA-listed disease-associated variants across 192 affected dogs from 71 breeds to evaluate diagnostic utility and identify novel disease models. This led to the identification of a novel candidate duplication c.442dupC in the X-linked Retinoschisin 1 (RS1) gene, located in the conserved discoidin domain of RS1. If validated, this variant may establish the first spontaneous canine model for human X-linked retinoschisis that may provide a new model for studying pathogenesis and therapeutic approaches. AIM: To facilitate structure-function analysis by evaluating the compatibility of newly added 10 extra test points in early-stage glaucoma cases with optical coherence tomography (OCT) and OCT-angiography (OCTA) glaucoma parameters in clinical practice.

metas.texte: Glaucoma neurodegeneration: targeted modulation of intraocular immune pathways - a review of novel therapeutic advances.. Glaucoma is the leading global cause of irreversible blindness, with its pathogenesis extending far beyond elevated intraocular pressure. Dysregulation of the intraocular immune system plays a central role in the progressive death of retinal ganglion cells. This review systematically examines the research progress on key intraocular immune pathways in glaucomatous neurodegeneration, with a primary focus on immune-inflammatory responses mediated by microglia, astrocytes, and T cells. It delves into the molecular mechanisms of various immunoregulatory networks, including the TLR4/nuclear factor kappa B (TLR4/NF-κB), Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK/STAT), mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), complement, and T-cell receptor signaling pathways. metas.texte: The 1-2-3 Rule: When to "Consider" Glaucoma Surgery and Discuss It With Patients.. Earlier intervention is gaining momentum in glaucoma care, yet delayed referral and delayed consideration of surgery remain concerns in clinical practice. A simple clinical rule may help general ophthalmologists recognize when to discuss procedural options with patients. We propose the Shimane University 1-2-3 rule (SU1-2-3), comprising three prompts: intraocular pressure (IOP) >12 mmHg in progressive advanced glaucoma, with advanced glaucoma defined for this rule as visual field mean deviation ≤ -10 dB or glaucomatous visual field defects within the central 10°; IOP >20 mmHg despite topical treatment in perimetric glaucoma; or use of ≥3 bottles of IOP-lowering eye drops. Oral acetazolamide use is an additional, independent prompt. Meeting any criterion should initiate consideration of surgical options, shared decision-making, and specialist consultation when appropriate, rather than constitute an automatic indication for surgery. metas.titre: Integration of biomarkers in common retinal neurodegenerative diseases: a comprehensive review.
metas.texte: Integration of biomarkers in common retinal neurodegenerative diseases: a comprehensive review.. Retinal neurodegenerative diseases (RNDs) are major causes of irreversible vision loss worldwide. RNDs majorly include age-related macular degeneration (AMD), diabetic retinopathy (DR), and glaucoma. Despite their distinct etiologies, these conditions share convergent mechanisms of retinovascular ischemia, neuronal apoptosis, and chronic inflammation. Physiologically, the retina and optic nerve are direct extensions of the central nervous system, sharing embryological origin, glial architecture, and neurodegenerative mechanisms with the brain, positioning them as an accessible model system for studying both ocular and systemic neurodegeneration. The growing field of ocular biomarkers thus offers objective, quantifiable endpoints for early detection, disease monitoring, and therapeutic evaluation of RNDs by bridging structural, functional, molecular, and genetic dimensions of retinal health. metas.texte: Psychiatry of ophthalmology: proposing the ophthalmo-psychiatric disorders framework.. We propose the ophthalmo-psychiatric disorders (OPD) framework as an organizing clinical and research model at the interface of vision science and mental health, and to synthesize, with wording calibrated to evidence strength, bidirectional relationships between ophthalmic disease, visual function, and psychiatric states. Visual impairment and common mental disorders co-distribute globally, with adults with vision loss showing roughly two-to three-fold higher prevalence of depressive and anxiety symptoms than visually normal peers.
