metas.texte: Topical Cyclosporine in Ophthalmology: Current Formulations, Clinical Applications, Advantages, and Limitations.. Cyclosporine A (CsA) is a calcineurin-inhibiting immunomodulator that suppresses T cell-mediated inflammation, a central mechanism in the pathogenesis of many ocular surface diseases. Following the systemic use of CsA in ophthalmology, topical formulations were developed to provide local immunomodulation at the ocular surface while keeping systemic absorption negligible. Since the approval of the first commercial ophthalmic emulsion in 2002, topical CsA has become a cornerstone disease-modifying therapy. Unlike corticosteroids, topical CsA provides sustained anti-inflammatory control without the long-term risks of glaucoma and cataract. Its highly lipophilic and poorly water-soluble nature, however, has posed a persistent formulation challenge, driving the development of diverse delivery platforms, including anionic and cationic oil-in-water emulsions, aqueous nanomicellar and nanoemulsion solutions, and water-free semifluorinated alkane vehicles. Reading disability is a common and clinically relevant, yet under-recognized, functional impairment in glaucoma, with significant impact on independence, daily activities, and quality of life, particularly in an increasingly digital environment. Reading performance is influenced by a complex interplay of visual field loss, reduced contrast sensitivity, oculomotor dysfunction, and cognitive load. Patients typically exhibit reduced reading speed, increased fixation instability, and altered saccadic patterns, even in the presence of preserved visual acuity. The severity and spatial distribution of visual field defects play a key role in determining impairment, as central and paracentral defects may disrupt fixation and letter recognition, while peripheral loss can impair text navigation and eye movement guidance. metas.titre: On-going retinal neuronal degeneration despite clinical stability in glaucoma.
metas.texte: On-going retinal neuronal degeneration despite clinical stability in glaucoma.. Glaucoma, a leading cause of irreversible blindness, involves progressive retinal ganglion cell loss. Early detection of this neurodegeneration is critical, yet current clinical methods often identify disease only after substantial damage has occurred. This preliminary study used high-resolution adaptive optics-optical coherence tomography (AO-OCT) to track individual retinal ganglion cells in patients and healthy volunteers over 3 to 5 years. Results revealed higher neurodegeneration in glaucoma compared to normal aging. We observed 4.16 to 6.86% annual decrease in cell density in glaucoma, far exceeding the 0.27% cell loss rate observed in the healthy volunteer group. Critically, AO-OCT detected progression significantly earlier, identifying cell loss 0.74 years before conventional OCT and 1.49 years before visual field testing. These findings demonstrate AO-OCT as a more sensitive tool capable of monitoring glaucomatous damage with superior precision, potentially representing a major advancement over current clinical imaging.

metas.titre: IOP-independent treatment for neurodegeneration in glaucoma using optimized ROS-scavenging microparticles for sustained release of erythropoietin.
metas.texte: IOP-independent treatment for neurodegeneration in glaucoma using optimized ROS-scavenging microparticles for sustained release of erythropoietin.. Glaucoma is a slow-progressing neurodegenerative disease of the optic projection to the brain and a leading cause of blindness worldwide. Current treatments are targeted towards lowering intraocular pressure (IOP), the only known, modifiable risk factor; however, this strategy is ineffective in many patients. An early hallmark of glaucomatous neurodegeneration is increased reactive oxygen species (ROS), representing an alternative opportunity for intervention to halt or slow disease progression. In this work, we optimize a ROS-scavenging copolymer, poly(propylene sulfide-co-ethylene sulfide) (PPSES), for formulation of size-controlled, stabilized, antioxidant microparticles (MPs) for sustained release of the protein erythropoietin (EPO). EPO promotes biological antioxidant defense via activation of NRF2-mediated transcription of antioxidant genes. Bilateral interstitial keratitis following intracameral Durysta® (bimatoprost).. PURPOSE: To report a case of bilateral interstitial keratitis following repeat intracameral bimatoprost injections.
OBSERVATIONS: A 92-year-old female with advanced primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) and poor adherence to topical glaucoma medications received bilateral intracameral Durysta® (bimatoprost) implants twelve months apart. Four months following the second intracameral injections, she developed bilateral interstitial keratitis (IK) as evidenced by keratitic precipitates and deep corneal stromal vascularization on slit lamp examination. There was no history of prior herpetic keratitis or blepharoconjunctivitis, and syphilis testing was negative. The patient was treated with valacyclovir and prednisolone acetate, with subsequent slow improvement in her corneal findings.
CONCLUSIONS AND IMPORTANCE: This case highlights a rare adverse event following repeated intracameral bimatoprost implants. metas.texte:
Predicting Future Visual Field Status from Baseline OCT Scan in Early to Moderate Glaucoma Using Deep Learning.. OBJECTIVE: The visual field (VF) test results of many eyes with glaucoma progress despite treatment. This suggests that some eyes are either untreated or that the management of intraocular pressure does not influence the outcome. In this work, we explore whether future VF parameters can be predicted from a baseline OCT-retinal nerve fiber layer (OCT-RNFL) scan using a deep learning model.
DESIGN: Retrospective multicenter cohort study with external validation.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 1792 eyes from 1610 patients were used for model development. External validation was performed on 150 eyes from a second center (Zeiss Cirrus OCT) and 280 eyes from a third center (Heidelberg Spectralis OCT).
METHODS: A Vision Transformer (ViT)-based regression model was trained on baseline OCT-RNFL scans to predict 3 key VF indices (follow-up interval: 4.74 ± 2.59 years). Model performance was evaluated using regression metrics with 95% confidence intervals. Saliency maps were generated to identify OCT-RNFL regions for making decisions in predicting functional visual status.

BACKGROUND: Ocular morbidity remains poorly characterized among prisoners; this systematic review and meta-analysis quantified its prevalence, spectrum and associated factors across sub-Saharan Africa (SSA).
METHODS: This review followed a published Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA) Protocols (PRISMA-P) and searched eight databases using prespecified terms, with study selection guided by PRISMA. Data were standardized and synthesized using random-effects meta-analysis to estimate pooled prevalence with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with heterogeneity assessed using I 2 and sensitivity and condition-specific analyses used to assess variation.
RESULTS: Six studies comprising 3,361 participants from four SSA countries, Nigeria, Uganda, Tanzania and Kenya, met the inclusion criteria. The pooled prevalence of ocular morbidity was 43.1% (95% CI: 12.4-77.1%; I 2 = 99.2%). Temporal trends in radiation-induced optic neuropathy: a meta-analysis.. BACKGROUND: Radiation-induced optic neuropathy (RION) is a rare but disabling toxicity. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate temporal trends in the incidence of RION according to advances in radiotherapy techniques and fractionation schemes over time.
METHODS: A systematic search identified 1994-2025 studies reporting optic neuropathy in patients after radiotherapy (hereby defined as RION). Data on RION incidence, diagnostic criteria, ocular or extraocular tumor, radiotherapy modality, conventional fractionation or hypofractionation, and modeling strategies were extracted. Random effects meta-analysis was performed to estimate pooled incidence rates and assess heterogeneity.

CASE SERIES: We report six immunocompetent adults who experienced delayed diagnosis and deferred targeted therapy for CMV corneal endotheliitis at Ho Chi Minh City Eye Hospital. The primary objective of this report is to delineate the distinct clinical trajectories culminating in misdiagnosis. Early fine-needle aspiration was limited by low cellularity and lack of ocular pathology review, yielding a small nonspecific lymphoid population insufficient for diagnosis. metas.titre: Angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) drives human Tenon's capsule fibroblast activation and myofibroblast transformation via the RhoA/ROCK signaling pathway.
metas.texte: Angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) drives human Tenon's capsule fibroblast activation and myofibroblast transformation via the RhoA/ROCK signaling pathway.. Although the angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) participates in systemic tissue remodeling, its exact contribution to human subconjunctival fibrosis remains poorly understood. This study investigated the expression of AT1R in human clinical scar specimens, the downstream involvement of the RhoA/ROCK pathway, and the independent anti-fibrotic effects of receptor blockade. Primary human Tenon's capsule fibroblasts (HTCFs) were isolated from patient tissue biopsies and verified as a pure mesenchymal lineage using immunofluorescence and quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR). To model the scar microenvironment, primary cells were stimulated with transforming growth factor-beta 1 (TGF-β1), either alone or in combination with Angiotensin II, the AT1R antagonist Olmesartan (OMS), or the selective ROCK inhibitor Y-27,632. Profibrotic and structural markers, including AT1R, alpha-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA), RhoA, ROCK1, fibronectin, and collagen I alpha (COL1A1), were quantified via Western blotting, qRT-PCR and immunofluorescence.

metas.texte: Role of smartphone-based digital adherence support for glaucoma medication therapy.. Sustained adherence to intraocular pressure-lowering medications is essential for preventing progressive visual loss in patients with glaucoma on pharmacotherapy. However, adherence remains suboptimal across patient populations as the result of cognitive, behavioural, physical, and socioeconomic barriers. Recent advances in digital health have introduced smartphone-based adherence supports intended to reinforce glaucoma medication routines, improve treatment organization, and support self-management. This narrative review synthesises evidence examining smartphone-based reminder applications and related digital adherence supports in glaucoma care, with attention to usability, patient experience, behavioural determinants, and clinical feasibility. Preliminary studies have reported improvements in short-term self-reported adherence and glaucoma-specific quality of life, particularly among patients with low baseline adherence. Understanding these complex interactions requires dissecting apart its cellular and molecular drivers. To tease apart the molecular links coupling retinogenesis to vascular development, we utilized conditional knockout mouse models to selectively delete the transcription factor T-box 3 ( Tbx3 ) in 1) astrocytes, 2) postnatal retinal ganglion cells (RGCs), or 3) retinal progenitors. We demonstrate that the hypovascular retina phenotype observed upon Tbx3 loss most likely stems from a disruption of early retinogenesis. METHODS: Data were obtained from the Global Burden of Disease 2021 study. metas.texte:
Artificial intelligence in glaucoma diagnosis and management: a systematic review of the past decade (2015-2026).. INTRODUCTION: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being used to support glaucoma detection and monitoring, with rapid advances in deep learning, multimodal imaging, and longitudinal prediction. This review evaluates the evidence supporting these developments and identifies barriers to clinical translation.
AREAS COVERED: A systematic search of PubMed, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, and SpringerLink was conducted following PRISMA guidelines, with the protocol registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261450819). Of 3,758 records identified, 63 eligible peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2026 were included. The review examined AI techniques, imaging modalities, datasets, diagnostic and predictive performance, validation strategies, and reported limitations in Glaucoma care. Most studies used deep learning applied to fundus photography, optical coherence tomography (OCT), OCT angiography, visual fields, or multimodal data. Many models achieved an area under the ROC curve of approximately 0.95.

Transplantation of induced pluripotent stem cell-derived retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) is a promising strategy for optic nerve regeneration and vision restoration in glaucoma. However, injections of conventional single-cell suspensions have low engraftment rates, hindering the formation of the complex neural circuits essential for functional recovery. This study addresses this challenge by investigating an in vitro biomimetic tissue engineering approach designed for future translational objectives, such as RGC transplantation therapy. We systematically evaluated coating materials and culture supplements critical for the survival and morphological development of RGCs on biocompatible, aligned poly-ε-caprolactone (PCL) nanofiber membranes. metas.titre: A Novel Intronic OCRL1 Variant Causing Lowe Syndrome with an Atypical Phenotype Mimicking Mucopolysaccharidosis.
metas.texte: A Novel Intronic OCRL1 Variant Causing Lowe Syndrome with an Atypical Phenotype Mimicking Mucopolysaccharidosis.. Lowe syndrome is a rare X-linked recessive multisystem disorder caused by pathogenic OCRL1 variants. We describe a 19-month-old child with global developmental delay, bilateral congenital cataracts, glaucoma, and hypotonia but without clinically apparent renal involvement at last follow-up. Brain and spine magnetic resonance imaging revealed scaphocephaly, a J-shaped sella, peritrigonal white-matter abnormalities, and a soft-tissue lesion causing compression at the craniovertebral junction, suggestive of mucopolysaccharidosis. Whole-exome sequencing (WES) identified a novel pathogenic hemizygous splice-site variant, c. 1880-2A > G, in OCRL1 . This case highlights the atypical phenotype of Lowe syndrome, which mimics mucopolysaccharidosis, and the diagnostic utility of WES in such presentations.

Doyne honeycomb retinal dystrophy with primary angle closure: a case report.. OBJECTIVE: To report a clinical case of Doyne honeycomb retinal dystrophy (DHRD) caused by an EFEMP1 gene mutation complicated by primary angle closure, and to discuss its clinical characteristics, reasons for misdiagnosis, and therapeutic challenges.
METHODS: The clinical data of a 53-year-old male patient were retrospectively analyzed. The patient presented with binocular metamorphopsia and decreased visual acuity persisting for over 9 years. He had been previously misdiagnosed with "macular degeneration" and "macular edema" and received corresponding treatments for a prolonged period. During the current consultation, multimodal fundus imaging (FFA/ICGA/OCT), ultrasound biomicroscopy (UBM), and ophthalmic genetic testing were performed.
RESULTS: Fundus examination and imaging revealed characteristic radial drusen in the posterior pole and nasal to the optic disc, retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) atrophy, and secondary choroidal neovascularization (CNV) in the macular region. metas.titre: Outcome of gonioscopy-assisted transluminal trabeculotomy in glaucoma: 5-year results.
metas.texte:
Outcome of gonioscopy-assisted transluminal trabeculotomy in glaucoma: 5-year results.. OBJECTIVE: Gonioscopy-assisted transluminal trabeculotomy (GATT) has gained popularity as a microinvasive glaucoma surgery procedure, yet long-term outcomes remain understudied. Our study evaluated the 5-year efficacy and safety of GATT.
DESIGN: Multicentre retrospective cohort study.
PATIENTS: Adult patients with open-angle glaucoma who underwent GATT with or without phacoemulsification between 2016 and 2019 were included. We excluded eyes with previous glaucoma surgery, angle-closure, or traumatic glaucoma.
METHODS: The primary outcome was surgical success, defined as the absence of a need for reoperation or a laser procedure for uncontrolled intraocular pressure (IOP) or disease progression. Secondary outcomes additionally required IOP thresholds of ≤21, ≤18 and ≤15 mm Hg without an increase in anti-glaucoma medication (AGM) use. Five-year changes in IOP, AGM use, best-corrected visual acuity, OCT parameters, and adverse events also were assessed.
RESULTS: In total, 74 eyes from 62 patients (mean age 59.1 ± 13.9 years; 54% male) were analysed, including 56 standalone GATT and 18 Phaco-GATT ca

metas.titre: Late-onset filtering bleb complications: A review.
metas.texte: Late-onset filtering bleb complications: A review.. Late-onset filtering bleb dysfunction remains an important determinant of long-term outcomes following glaucoma filtration surgery. Although trabeculectomy provides sustained intraocular pressure (IOP) reduction, progressive changes in bleb architecture and wound healing can result in filtration failure, hypotony, leakage, ocular discomfort, and sight-threatening infection. This review examines the clinical characteristics, underlying mechanisms, assessment, prevention, and management of late-onset bleb complications, with emphasis on individualized, mechanism-directed care. Standardized bleb grading systems facilitate documentation of morphology and longitudinal assessment. Anterior segment optical coherence tomography and ultrasound biomicroscopy complement clinical examination by delineating bleb architecture and identifying potential sites of outflow obstruction, while optical coherence tomography angiography offers an evolving approach to evaluating bleb vascularity. Elevated IOP may arise from internal ostial obstruction, scleral flap adhesion, subconjunctival fibrosis, or encapsulation. Management depends on the site and ex

metas.titre: A diagnostic challenge: syphilitic optic neuropathy.
metas.texte: A diagnostic challenge: syphilitic optic neuropathy.. Syphilitic optic neuropathy is an uncommon but treatable cause of visual loss and may occur as an isolated manifestation of neurosyphilis. We report a 72-year-old man who presented with progressive painless unilateral visual loss. He was initially diagnosed as non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy but later developed progressive worsening, optic nerve MRI abnormalities and delayed visual evoked potentials. Other causes of optic neuropathies, such as demyelination were considered. Despite immunotherapy, vision continued to deteriorate. Subsequent investigations demonstrated positive serum VDRL and TPPA. With the exclusion of other causes of chronic optic neuropathy, syphilitic optic neuropathy was diagnosed. Treatment with intravenous benzylpenicillin stabilized vision, although established optic atrophy prevented visual recovery. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges and emphasizes the importance of routine syphilis serology in atypical, progressive, or treatment-refractory optic neuropathies.

metas.titre: Determining the Quality of Functional Evidence for Coding Variants in CYP1B1 for Use in Variant Classification.
metas.texte: Determining the Quality of Functional Evidence for Coding Variants in CYP1B1 for Use in Variant Classification.. Biallelic variants in the CYP1B1 gene are associated with primary congenital glaucoma and some instances of anterior segment dysgenesis and juvenile open-angle glaucoma. Genetic testing is increasingly used in the diagnosis of these conditions and to inform future family planning decisions. Variant-specific functional data play a critical role in variant classification during the interpretation of genetic test results. In this study, the ClinGen Glaucoma Variant Curation Expert Panel (VCEP) evaluated published functional assays assessing CYP1B1 protein stability and enzymatic activity to determine which assays meet the recommended standards for use in variant classification, specifically when applying the PS3 or BS3 criteria from the ACMG/AMP variant interpretation guidelines. Following a comprehensive literature review, the panel identified assays that examined protein abundance and stability, as well as enzymatic activity across a range of substrates. metas.titre: Cross-organ translation of antifibrotic strategies from skin and lung fibrosis to glaucoma filtration surgery.
metas.texte: Cross-organ translation of antifibrotic strategies from skin and lung fibrosis to glaucoma filtration surgery.. Filtering bleb scarring after glaucoma filtration surgery (GFS) remains the leading cause of surgical failure, and current antimetabolites are limited by non-selective cytotoxicity that restricts their long-term use. Research on skin and lung fibrosis has accumulated extensive experience in antifibrotic mechanisms and therapeutic approaches. These tissues share a common transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β)-driven program of fibroblast activation and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling with Tenon capsule fibroblasts, providing a theoretical basis for translating antifibrotic strategies across organs. From a cross-organ translational medicine perspective, this review systematically summarizes progress in translating antifibrotic research from skin and lung fibrosis to antiscarring therapy for GFS, focusing on four aspects: shared fibrotic mechanisms; repurposed approved drugs and emerging molecular targets; local drug delivery systems (DDS); and ophthalmology-specific translational challenges. metas.titre: Translational lipidomics in glaucoma: mechanisms, biomarkers, and therapeutic horizons.
metas.texte: Translational lipidomics in glaucoma: mechanisms, biomarkers, and therapeutic horizons.. Glaucoma is a multifactorial optic neuropathy. Intraocular pressure (IOP), aging, vascular dysregulation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial failure, and chronic neuroinflammation converge on retinal ganglion cell (RGC) degeneration and optic nerve damage. Lipid mediators are central to this biology, linking membrane remodeling to aqueous humor (AH) dynamics, glial activation, vascular tone, extracellular matrix turnover, and neuronal survival. Lipidomics has widened the field beyond prostaglandin pharmacology to include oxylipins, lysophospholipids, sphingolipids, endocannabinoids, and specialized pro-resolving mediators (SPMs). Human studies in AH, tears, and plasma report reproducible perturbations in arachidonic acid (AA) metabolism, oxidized linoleate products, phosphatidylcholines, lysophosphatidylcholines, sphingomyelins, and ceramides; experimental models further implicate ceramide accumulation, phospholipase A2 activation, cyclooxygenase signaling, endocannabinoid tone, and failed inflammation resolution in retinal injury. metas.texte: Discharge Readiness After Ophthalmic Day Surgery: A Patient-Centered Perspective on Nursing Assessment, Self-Management, and Adherence.. Medical eligibility for discharge after ophthalmic day surgery does not establish whether patients can manage recovery at home. This conceptual Perspective uses Transition Theory to examine how nursing assessment can connect discharge preparation with practical self-management tasks. The pathway adapts established discharge-preparation and transitional-care principles by specifying ophthalmic tasks to verify, incorporating patient preferences into feasible support arrangements, and linking unresolved deficits to reassessment and follow-up. Relevant tasks include eye-drop administration, understanding changes to treatment, recognising warning symptoms, and carrying out prescribed positioning or restrictions. Direct readiness evidence remains predominantly cataract-based, with additional observational evidence from vitreoretinal day surgery; glaucoma and corneal studies provide adjacent evidence on postoperative care and adherence. metas.texte:
Polypseudophakia with the J&J synergy lens in high myopia: case report.. INTRODUCTION AND IMPORTANCE: As clinicians strive to provide personalized recommendations for patients, polypseudophakia may be an option for those outside the range of traditional extended depth-of-focus lenses. We describe a case with initial refractive success but the development of a potentially vision-threatening complication.
PRESENTATION OF CASE: A 40-year-old Asian man with high myopia presented for a refractive surgery consultation with a goal of total spectacle independence and underwent bilateral refractive lens exchange with the J&J Synergy lens in the capsular bag, and a minus-power Alcon MA60MA lens in the sulcus. Initially, there was refractive success with post-operative uncorrected distance vision of 20/20 in the right eye and 20/25 in the left eye at 6 months. However, both eyes developed transillumination defects with pigment in the anterior chamber, consistent with Uveitis-Glaucoma-Hyphema (UGH) syndrome. The patient ultimately elected bilateral explantation of the sulcus intraocular lenses (IOLs) due to this complication.

metas.titre: Difficult strabismus surgery following subconjunctival silicone oil migration: a case report.
metas.texte:
Difficult strabismus surgery following subconjunctival silicone oil migration: a case report.. INTRODUCTION AND IMPORTANCE: Subconjunctival migration of silicone oil is a rare but clinically significant complication following vitreoretinal surgery. The resulting inflammation and fibrosis can increase the difficulty of subsequent ocular operations, such as strabismus surgery. Understanding this phenomenon is crucial for preventing intraoperative complications and ensuring better surgical outcomes.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 26-year-old female presented with sensory exotropia in the right eye following multiple vitreoretinal surgeries involving silicone oil tamponade. During strabismus surgery, multiple subconjunctival cysts filled with silicone oil and extensive fibrosis were encountered, particularly around the rectus muscle insertions. The procedure required extensive dissection and hemostasis, prolonging operative time. Despite intraoperative challenges, the postoperative ocular alignment achieved orthotropia in the primary position, with satisfactory cosmetic results.

Axial Length-Dependent Macular Choroidal Topography in POAG: A Wide-Field Swept-Source Optical Coherence Tomography Study.. PURPOSE: To characterize the topography of the macular choroidal thickness (mCT) in POAG across axial lengths (AXLs), and to determine the clinical factors associated with the mCT.
METHODS: Wide-field swept-source optical coherence tomography with a 30 × 30 macular grid (6 mm × 6 mm) was used to generate spatial maps of the mCT and macular ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer thickness (mGCIPLT). The mCT was compared pointwise between POAG and control eyes, and cluster-based permutation testing was used to assess topographic significance in the entire cohort and in three subgroups stratified by AXL (<24.5 mm, 24.5-26.0 mm, and ≥26.0 mm). Clinical factors associated with the mCT were evaluated using regression analyses.
RESULTS: This study included 117 POAG eyes and 157 control eyes. While the mCT was only marginally thinner in POAG eyes than in controls, topographic analyses of the mCT revealed areas of localized thinning in the papillomacular and inferotemporal peripapillary areas in POAG, which did not overlap with the pattern of mGCIPLT reduction. metas.titre: Electrical stimulation targeting optic nerve regeneration following acute and chronic neuropathies.
metas.texte: Electrical stimulation targeting optic nerve regeneration following acute and chronic neuropathies.. Optic neuropathies such as glaucoma or optic neuritis are conditions whereby the optic nerve is damaged by mechanisms including ischemia, compression, inflammation or immune-mediated processes, leading to progressive degeneration of retinal ganglion cells and subsequent loss of vision. Strategies including medication and surgery help to slow down these diseases but fail to repair the neurons of the optic nerve themselves. In this review, we first detail the range of optic nerve neuropathies and their current front line treatment options, briefly outline various experimental treatment strategies and their limitations, before focusing on electrical stimulation as a treatment strategy, covering the current state of the art and potential routes for further development.

metas.titre: Assessment setting affects the evaluation of functional mobility in older adults with glaucoma.
metas.texte:
Assessment setting affects the evaluation of functional mobility in older adults with glaucoma.. BACKGROUND: Older adults with glaucoma are at a greater risk of falls than those without, and visual field loss is associated with mobility limitations and fall risk. In-clinic gait assessments can identify those with mobility limitations, but these tools are underused in routine glaucoma care. Further, it remains unknown if gait measured in clinic is associated with gait in everyday environments for older adults with glaucoma.
METHODS: In this pilot study, older adults with glaucoma (n = 36, 77 ± 5 years) completed a 2-minute walk test in the clinic and then in their home. Participants wore three inertial measurement units, and spatiotemporal gait metrics were computed from this data. In-clinic and at-home gait metrics were compared to test the effect of setting and whether at-home gait metrics were associated with in-clinic metrics.

metas.titre: Risk of angle-closure glaucoma after lens extraction versus laser peripheral iridotomy in primary angle-closure suspects.
metas.texte:
Risk of angle-closure glaucoma after lens extraction versus laser peripheral iridotomy in primary angle-closure suspects.. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between lens extraction versus laser peripheral iridotomy (LPI) and progression from primary angle-closure suspect (PACS) to coded angle-closure glaucoma (ACG).
DESIGN: Retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study.
PARTICIPANTS: Patients with PACS undergoing lens extraction or LPI (January 2014 to February 2026) in the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network and matched 1:1 on demographics, systemic and ocular comorbidities, medications, and body mass index, yielding 6059 patients per group (mean age, 68 years; 69% female; 59% White).
METHODS: The primary outcome was a new coded ACG diagnosis assessed using Cox regression. Prespecified subgroup analyses by age (<60, 60-70, >70 years) and sex used separately matched cohorts, with optic neuritis as a negative control outcome.
RESULTS: Coded ACG occurred in 3.5% of the lens-extraction group versus 5.4% of the LPI group (hazard ratio [HR] 0.66, 95% CI 0.56-0.79, P < 0.001). A significant benefit was observed in patients >70 years (HR 0.62, P < 0.001), but not in patients <

metas.titre: Chronic Topical Water-Soluble Cannabidiol Formulation Reduces Intraocular Pressure and Corneal Mechanical Sensitivity in DBA/2J Mice.
metas.texte: Chronic Topical Water-Soluble Cannabidiol Formulation Reduces Intraocular Pressure and Corneal Mechanical Sensitivity in DBA/2J Mice.. Glaucoma is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disease and a leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide. Although elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) is the main modifiable risk factor, current therapies often fail to fully prevent disease progression and may cause ocular discomfort. Cannabidiol (CBD) has attracted increasing interest due to its anti-inflammatory, analgesic and vasoregulatory properties, yet its ocular effects remain controversial, partly due to formulation-dependent limitations and short-term administration paradigms. We evaluated a novel water-soluble topical CBD formulation in a spontaneous murine model of glaucoma (DBA/2J mice), using CD-1 mice as a non-glaucomatous comparator strain. IOP, tear production, corneal mechanical sensitivity and body weight were assessed longitudinally in conscious animals following acute and chronic CBD administration (once or twice daily). metas.titre: [Multiple mechanisms and intervention strategies of monocytes/macrophages in ocular diseases].
metas.texte: [Multiple mechanisms and intervention strategies of monocytes/macrophages in ocular diseases].. Monocytes/macrophages possess prominent heterogeneity and functional plasticity, and their functional imbalance participates in the initiation and progression of multiple ocular diseases. This review summarizes the roles of monocytes/macrophages in age-related macular degeneration, diabetic retinopathy, high myopia, uveitis and glaucoma. It particularly elaborates their pathogenic mechanisms involving oxidative stress, inflammatory amplification, blood-retinal barrier disruption and pathological neovascularization, alongside their immunomodulatory and tissue-repairing functions. We also outline intervention strategies targeting monocytes/macrophages, including blocking pro-inflammatory recruitment and signaling pathways, inducing anti-inflammatory polarization, and immune reprogramming, which may offer novel ideas for precision therapy of chronic inflammatory ocular diseases.

metas.titre: Piezo1 mechanobiology in high myopia and glaucoma: compartment-specific evidence, gaps, and a hypothesis-generating susceptibility framework.
metas.texte: Piezo1 mechanobiology in high myopia and glaucoma: compartment-specific evidence, gaps, and a hypothesis-generating susceptibility framework.. High myopia and glaucoma are clinically distinct but mechanobiologically connected conditions. High myopia is commonly associated with marked axial elongation, posterior-segment stretch, scleral remodeling, and altered posterior-pole and peripapillary biomechanics, whereas glaucoma involves intraocular pressure (IOP)-related outflow stress, optic nerve head (ONH) strain, and retinal ganglion cell (RGC) vulnerability. Both disorders therefore converge on chronic mechanical stress and compartment-specific susceptibility. Piezo1, a mechanically activated cation channel, is well positioned to connect membrane tension, extracellular matrix (ECM) state, Ca2+ signaling, reactive oxygen species (ROS)-associated stress responses, and cellular remodeling. This review develops a hypothesis-driven but evidence-bound framework centered on a possible Piezo1-linked mechanobiological susceptibility axis between high myopia and glaucoma. metas.titre: Glaucoma in Somalia: From Late Presentation to Prevention, Building a National Pathway for Glaucoma Care.
metas.texte: Glaucoma in Somalia: From Late Presentation to Prevention, Building a National Pathway for Glaucoma Care.. Glaucoma is a major cause of irreversible vision loss for which timely detection and sustained treatment can reduce disease progression. In Somalia, a tertiary eye-clinic study reported primary open-angle glaucoma in 7% of 1550 attendees older than 40 years, while a community outreach report classified 9% of 628 screened participants as having glaucoma risk; 28 people were referred for glaucoma evaluation. These estimates arise from different selected populations, use different case definitions, and are not comparable estimates of national prevalence. A recent tertiary-center study also identified glaucoma among causes of adult blindness. This commentary proposes a six-stage, integrated glaucoma care pathway for Somalia: awareness and risk recognition, primary-level detection, referral and referral refinement, specialist confirmation, individualized treatment, and continued follow-up. metas.titre: Effect of Eye Movement and Body Position on Optic Nerve Sheath Width.
metas.texte:
Effect of Eye Movement and Body Position on Optic Nerve Sheath Width.. PURPOSE: Orbital cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) dynamics are poorly understood but are postulated to play a role in several optic nerve pathologies. This study aims to evaluate the effects of eye movement and body position on perioptic CSF clearance by optic nerve sheath width (ONSW) measurement.
METHODS: Healthy adult patients were recruited prospectively from an outpatient ophthalmology clinic at an academic center. B-mode ultrasound was used to measure optic nerve sheath width (ONSW) 3 mm posterior to the optic disc after 5 minutes of no eye movement (-EM) and 1 minute of eye movement (+EM) in three body positions: upright, supine, and prone. CSF clearance is the difference between ONSW +EM and -EM in each body position.
RESULTS: Thirty-eight adults with healthy optic nerves were recruited. ONSW -EM were significantly wider than +EM in all three positions (P = 0.002, 0.024, 0.002). Body positioning only significantly affected ONSW -EM (P = 0.030), while +EM ONSW was not significantly different in any body position, indicating a baseline effect.

metas.titre: Unilateral Angle Closure as the Initial Presentation of Multiple Myeloma Metastasis.
metas.texte:
Unilateral Angle Closure as the Initial Presentation of Multiple Myeloma Metastasis.. PURPOSE: Ocular manifestations of multiple myeloma (MM) are rare but may affect all tissues of the eye. This report describes a patient with recurrent MM initially presenting with ocular hypertension due to angle closure, revealing extensive ocular, orbital, and systemic metastatic disease.
CASE REPORT: A 54-year-old female patient with previously treated MM presented with left eye pain, blurred vision, and an intraocular pressure of 38 mmHg. Examination revealed proptosis, restricted upward gaze, conjunctival injection with two salmon-patch lesions, and complete angle closure. Further findings included multiple ciliary body cysts, a massive choroidal mass, and retinal/choroidal detachments. She had pancytopenia. Magnetic resonance imaging confirmed recurrent MM with superior rectus muscle and spine infiltrations, and a large prevertebral lymph node mass. The patient responded well to antiglaucoma medications and was referred to her oncologist.
CONCLUSION: MM can involve various ophthalmic structures. Patients with MM require regular examinations for early detection of ocular metastasis.

metas.titre: Gut-hormone receptor systems in the eye: Pharmacological, local and putative endocrine signalling.
metas.texte: Gut-hormone receptor systems in the eye: Pharmacological, local and putative endocrine signalling.. The neural retina has traditionally been viewed as a downstream target of systemic metabolic disease, yet experimental and clinical evidence suggests that ocular tissues may also respond directly to peptide-hormone signalling. This review critically examines gut-hormone-related receptor systems in the eye across three biologically distinct evidence streams: endogenous circulating gut peptides, pharmacological receptor agonism, and locally synthesised ocular peptides. Physiological retinal access of native gut peptides remains poorly characterised, while receptor localisation is highly dependent on species and detection methodology. Mechanistic evidence is strongest for pharmacological GLP-1 receptor activation and local NPY and ghrelin systems, particularly in relation to neuroprotection, immunomodulation, metabolic and oxidative homeostasis, and neurovascular regulation. metas.titre: Incidence and Management of Ocular Hypertension Following the 0.19 mg Fluocinolone Acetonide Implant for Diabetic Macular Edema.
metas.texte:
Incidence and Management of Ocular Hypertension Following the 0.19 mg Fluocinolone Acetonide Implant for Diabetic Macular Edema.. PURPOSE: To investigate the real-world incidence and management of ocular hypertension (OHT) following the intravitreal 0.19 mg fluocinolone acetonide implant (FAi, Iluvien) for diabetic macular edema (DME).
METHODS: Retrospective review of eyes treated with FAi (2015-2025) with ≥1 month follow-up. Primary outcome was OHT (IOP >25 mmHg). Secondary outcomes included IOP >30 mmHg, IOP rise ≥10 mmHg from baseline, and OHT management.
RESULTS: A total of 118 eyes (90 patients) were included with mean follow-up of 33.1 ± 1.3 months. Mean baseline IOP was 14.0 ± 3.0 mmHg. Pre-existing glaucoma or OHT was present in 32.2% of eyes, and 78.8% had a prior periocular or intravitreal corticosteroid injection. Overall, 11 eyes (9.3%) developed OHT (IOP >25mmHg) following FAi. Peak IOP >30 mmHg occurred in 6 eyes (5.1%), and 12 eyes (10.2%) had an IOP rise ≥10 mmHg above baseline. metas.texte:
Staged surgical management of an acute angle-closure crisis with medically refractory intraocular pressure elevation: A case report and literature review.. RATIONALE: Acute angle closure with markedly elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) is an ocular emergency. Initial management aims to lower IOP, reduce corneal edema and inflammation, and permit definitive relief of pupillary block, usually by laser peripheral iridotomy (LPI). When IOP remains uncontrolled and corneal edema or an extremely shallow anterior chamber precludes safe LPI, urgent surgical intervention may be required.
PATIENT CONCERNS: A 61-year-old woman presented with a 7-hour history of pain, redness, and blurred vision in the right eye (RE), accompanied by headache.
DIAGNOSES: Acute primary angle closure in the RE and primary angle-closure suspect status in the left eye (LE).
INTERVENTIONS: During initial treatment with topical pilocarpine, carteolol, and brinzolamide, IOP in the RE increased from 32 to 58 mm Hg. metas.titre: Do Adjunctive Anti-scarring Agents Including Mitomycin-C Improve Glaucoma Tube Shunt Surgery: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
metas.texte:
Do Adjunctive Anti-scarring Agents Including Mitomycin-C Improve Glaucoma Tube Shunt Surgery: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.. PURPOSE: Adjunctive anti-scarring agents (ASAs), including mitomycin C (MMC), 5-Fluorouracil (5FU), corticosteroids and vascular endothelial growth factor antagonists (anti-VEGF), aim to improve glaucoma tube shunt (GTS) surgery by attenuating peri-endplate fibrosis. While used in trabeculectomy, ASAs are less established in GTS surgery, leading to varied practices. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated their efficacy and safety.
METHODS: Prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD 4,202,236,526), MEDLINE, EMBASE, and CENTRAL were searched for randomised controlled trials (RCTs) and comparative cohort studies (CCSs) comparing ASA and non-ASA use in GTS surgery. Outcomes included changes in intra-ocular pressure (IOP), anti-glaucoma medications, re-operation, and complication rates between baseline and post-operative months 3, 6, and 12.
RESULTS: 28 studies (n = 1621 eyes) were included: 12 RCTs (n = 624 eyes) and 16 CCSs (n = 997 eyes). ASAs included MMC (n = 11/28), corticosteroids (n = 7/28), Anti-VEGF (n = 6/28), and 5FU (n = 2/28). Two s

metas.titre: Timing of Glaucoma Drainage Device With Boston Keratoprosthesis
metas.texte:
Timing of Glaucoma Drainage Device With Boston Keratoprosthesis. Boston keratoprosthesis (KPro) is a piece of specialized plastic that replace sick cornea (transparent structure at the front of the eye) in patients who have failed or those who are expected to have poor results with traditional corneal transplantation. While the Kpro can offer dramatic improvement in vision, it is also associated with several complications. Glaucoma (optic nerve damage due to high pressure inside the eye) is one of the most common complications after KPro surgery and can potentially cause irreversible vision loss. The implantation of a glaucoma drainage device (GDD), a tiny tube that drains the liquid inside the eye by bypassing the natural drainage system, is an effective option to lower the eye pressure in patients with KPro. Given the frequency and potentially devastating effects of glaucoma among KPro patients, some surgeons recommend to put in a GDD as a preventative measure. However, there is no consensus on when is the best timing to perform such surgery in relation to the Boston Kpro surgery.

metas.titre: A More Engaging Visual Field Test to Increase Use and Reliability in Pediatrics
metas.texte: A More Engaging Visual Field Test to Increase Use and Reliability in Pediatrics. The majority of young children do not think that visual field (VF) testing of peripheral vision is similar to a game; therefore, it is not surprising that they have difficulty maintaining attention during VF testing and thus the test reliability suffers as a consequence. Poor VF reliability has been a longstanding, major issue since it leads to an increased number of tests and/or longer duration of time needed to determine when there are true vision losses. Providers are less likely to obtain VF tests in children since the results are of doubtful value and challenging to interpret when they are inconsistent. Effectively this means that children with untreated, slowly progressive eye diseases may go undiagnosed and incur greater visual losses. The investigators aim to create a prototype device that the investigators hypothesize will make VF testing more engaging for young children, thus increasing their attention and consistency of their responses to the test stimuli, which in turn should improve VF reliability. metas.titre: Impact of Glaucoma and Visual Field Loss on Life Space
metas.texte: Impact of Glaucoma and Visual Field Loss on Life Space. Mobility refers to a person's purposeful movement through the environment from one place to another and can be conceptualized as a continuum from bed bound (immobility) on one extreme to making excursions to distant locations on the other extreme. Primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) is a chronic, progressive optic neuropathy that can lead to gradual loss of vision in the peripheral field and central vision. Older adults with POAG have an increased risk for motor vehicle collisions and falls. Moreover, existing studies suggest that patients with POAG exhibit more postural sway while standing as measured by a balance platform and also tend to walk more slowly than those who are normally sighted and free of ocular disease. While these disturbances likely influence mobility, there has been little research directly assessing the impact of POAG on mobility. This study will assess the impact of POAG on life space (one aspect of mobility) and will determine whether difficulties with life space are associated with difficulties experienced under conditions of dim lighting.
