metas.texte: Multimodal Deep Learning for Humphrey 24-2 Visual Field Prediction: Evaluating the Contribution of Fellow-Eye Information in Glaucoma and Ocular Hypertension. Background/Objectives: To develop a multimodal deep learning framework for Humphrey 24-2 visual field prediction using multimodal OCT-derived structural information and to investigate whether incorporating fellow-eye information improves pointwise threshold sensitivity estimation in glaucoma and ocular hypertension. Methods: This retrospective study included 591 patients, 892 eyes, and 1099 eye-visit samples. Four OCT-derived image modalities were combined with demographic, optic disc, RNFL, and image-quality variables. Three architectures were evaluated using a patient-level 60/20/20 split: A0, a single-eye baseline; A1, bilateral Siamese feature fusion; and A2, fellow-eye-guided α-gated residual refinement applied exclusively to the 52-point threshold sensitivity output (TS52). Results: The baseline A0 model achieved MAEs of 2.97 dB (MD), 1.62 dB (PSD), and 3.26 dB (mean TS), with corresponding RMSEs of 4.40, 2.30, and 4.74 dB, respectively. metas.titre: Retinal organoid-derived exosomes enhance retinal ganglion cell survival in chronic ocular hypertension
metas.texte: Retinal organoid-derived exosomes enhance retinal ganglion cell survival in chronic ocular hypertension. Abstract Background To date, the therapeutic potential of retinal organoid–derived exosomes (Exo-ROs) for retinal ganglion cell (RGC) preservation in chronic ocular hypertension (COH) has not been explored. We aimed to evaluate the neuroprotective effects and underlying molecular mechanisms of Exo-ROs in a rat COH model. Methods Human induced pluripotent stem cell–derived retinal organoids (ROs) were differentiated, and exosomes were isolated from conditioned medium at day 60. COH was induced by circumlimbal suture in Sprague–Dawley rats, followed by intravitreal delivery of Exo-ROs. RGC survival and function were assessed by Brn3a immunostaining and photopic negative response (PhNR). To elucidate the mechanisms, MAPK pathway activation was analyzed at day 3, and total RNA sequencing was performed at 1 month post-treatment. Results Exo-ROs significantly improved RGC survival and preserved PhNR amplitudes in COH eyes ( p < 0.001). metas.titre: Interpretable AI plus Handheld, Portable Retinal Photographs: A Low-Cost Glaucoma Screening Solution for West Africa
metas.texte: Interpretable AI plus Handheld, Portable Retinal Photographs: A Low-Cost Glaucoma Screening Solution for West Africa. Purpose: To develop and evaluate an interpretable artificial intelligence (AI) framework for glaucoma screening from low-cost portable, handheld retinal fundus photographs in a West African population and to compare its performance with clinical tabletop fundus imaging. Methods: We used data from a community-based study of 681 participants (1,362 eyes) in Nigeria, comprising 414 glaucoma, 478 glaucoma suspect, and 470 non-glaucoma eyes. Fundus photographs were acquired using the low-cost handheld, portable Volk Viva retinal camera and the Canon CR-2-AF tabletop camera. We fine-tuned component models separately to each device to perform vessel segmentation, cup and disc boundary segmentation, and feature extraction to detect optic nerve head features. A final classification model combined these components to classify scans as glaucoma, glaucoma suspect or non-glaucoma. Feature-weight analysis and Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping were used for interpretation. metas.titre: ALLOSTATIC LOAD AND JUVENILE GLAUCOMA: A REVIEW
metas.texte: ALLOSTATIC LOAD AND JUVENILE GLAUCOMA: A REVIEW. Juvenile glaucoma is a rare but clinically important condition that may cause progressive optic nerve damage during childhood and adolescence. In addition to intraocular pressure (IOP), genetic predisposition and structural changes of the optic nerve, systemic physiological dysregulation may influence disease development and progression. Allostatic load (AL) reflects the cumulative physiological cost of repeated or chronic stress and integrates cardiovascular, metabolic, inflammatory and neuroendocrine components [1–3].

metas.texte: Evaluating global glaucoma awareness efforts: A study of World Glaucoma Week activities and influencing factors. Purpose To assess the global distribution of awareness and screening activities conducted during World Glaucoma Week (WGW) and to identify national-level factors associated with activity frequency. Design Cross-sectional observational study. Subjects Countries and cities reporting WGW activities (2015–2024) on the official WGW website. Methods Activity rates were standardized per 10,000 individuals with glaucoma-related blindness in each country. Pearson’s and Spearman’s correlation analysis was used to examine associations between WGW activity levels and national indicators, including the presence of a glaucoma society, the number of ophthalmologists, Gross Domestic Product (GDP), and Inequality-adjusted Human Development Index (IHDI) Results An average of 548.1 WGW activities were reported annually. Public education (30.9%) and awareness campaigns (30.2%) were the most frequently conducted activities. metas.texte: Automated Perimetry in Children with Suspected and Known Glaucoma: Virtual Reality Versus Tabletop. Abstract Humphrey visual field (HVF)-equivalent virtual reality fields (VRFs) have shown promise in adult glaucoma. Research comparing HVF-equivalent VRF to standard automated perimetry (SAP) in pediatric glaucoma is limited. We aimed to evaluate agreement and concordance between HVF-equivalent VRF and SAP for children with glaucoma. This prospective study enrolled children with known or suspected glaucoma. Participants completed HVF then VisuALL HVF-equivalent VRF at one visit. A masked ophthalmologist graded visual fields for defects and location. Global parameters were compared between devices. A point-by-point deviation plot analysis was performed. A total of 60 patients (116 eyes) were included, mean age 13.1 ± 2.93 years. Mean retinal nerve fiber layer thickness was 86.1 ± 21.20 µm. Average mean deviation (MD), pattern standard deviation (PSD), and foveal sensitivity significantly differed for HVF versus VRF. Abstract Purpose: To evaluate the long-term real-world efficacy, safety, and functional and structural outcomes in patients with ocular hypertension (OHT) or primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) undergoing trabecular micro-bypass surgery with the iStent inject W®. Methods: This retrospective longitudinal study included 149 eyes of 149 patients with OHT or POAG who underwent implantation of the iStent inject W®, combined with phacoemulsification, and were followed for up to five years. metas.titre: Augmentation Strategy for DINO in Glaucoma Classification
metas.texte: Augmentation Strategy for DINO in Glaucoma Classification. Self-supervised learning (SSL) offers a promising approach to medical image representation learning, yet augmentation strategies of SSL frameworks validated on natural images do not reliably transfer to specialized medical imaging domains. We analyze DINO, a knowledge-distillation based SSL framework, and empirically demonstrate that its default augmentation strategy produces unreliable representations for retinal fundus images, degrading downstream glaucoma classification performance. Guided by the principle that effective cropped views should share minimal redundant information while retaining clinically relevant signal, we redesign DINO's augmentation strategy. Our approach biases the learned representations toward diagnostically critical features rather than low-level image statistics. We evaluate our method for glaucoma classification by training a linear classifier on the frozen representations, achieving strong generalization across seven benchmark datasets. Background: This study aimed to investigate the relationship between the degree of visual impairment and depressive symptoms in patients with glaucoma, and examine whether disease duration moderates this relationship. Methods: We enrolled 208 patients with glaucoma who received standardised treatment at The Affiliated Huaian No.1 People’s Hospital of Nanjing Medical University from February 2022 to February 2025. Clinical data and visual function indicators were collected. Patient-reported visual function was assessed using the 25-item National Eye Institute Visual Function Questionnaire (NEI-VFQ-25), and depressive symptoms were assessed using the SelfRating Depression Scale (SDS). Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and central macular thickness (CMT) served as indicators of visual impairment. Introduction: Topical corticosteroids are routinely prescribed after cataract surgery to control postoperative inflammation. However, these agents may induce ocular hypertension, with a subset of individuals exhibiting significant Intraocular Pressure (IOP) elevation. metas.titre: Uveitis-associated glaucoma and treatment-requiring ocular hypertension in a tertiary referral center
metas.texte: Uveitis-associated glaucoma and treatment-requiring ocular hypertension in a tertiary referral center. Background: Elevated uveitis-associated intraocular pressure (IOP) may result from inflammatory, structural, and corticosteroid-related mechanisms and lead to secondary glaucoma. This study aimed to describe patients with uveitis who subsequently developed glaucoma or treatment-requiring ocular hypertension (OHT) in a tertiary referral clinic. Methods: This retrospective study was conducted at the Uveitis Clinic of Nikookari Eye Hospital, Tabriz University of Medical Sciences. Records of patients with uveitis diagnosed or managed during the preceding 10 years were reviewed. Patients were eligible if, after uveitis onset, they had IOP > 21 mmHg documented on at least two occasions separated by at least one week and requiring intervention, or documented glaucomatous findings based on available clinical assessment. metas.titre: TRACE: a framework for traceable biomedical resource construction demonstrated through single-cell glaucoma data
metas.texte: TRACE: a framework for traceable biomedical resource construction demonstrated through single-cell glaucoma data. The growing availability of public omics datasets presents opportunities for biomedical research, yet constructing research question-driven resources from distributed studies remains challenging due to heterogeneous data, incomplete metadata and limited documentation of curation decisions. Here, we present TRACE (Traceable Resource Assembly and Curation Ecosystem), a general framework that links systematic knowledge discovery, data curation and resource delivery while preserving provenance throughout resource construction. We demonstrate TRACE through TRACE-scGlaucoma, a curated single-cell transcriptomics resource for glaucoma and optic nerve biology. Systematic screening identified 57 eligible studies, of which 42 provided accessible datasets comprising approximately 3.3 million cells. The resource provides harmonised metadata, standardised cell-type annotations and reusable expression objects while retaining original study information and curation provenance. metas.titre: Glaucoma: Classification and Methods of Treatment, with Special Reference to Congenital and Secondary Glaucoma
metas.texte: Glaucoma: Classification and Methods of Treatment, with Special Reference to Congenital and Secondary Glaucoma. Glaucoma is a group of progressive optic neuropathies characterized by retinal ganglion-cell loss, structural damage to the optic nerve head and corresponding visual-field defects. Raised intraocular pressure (IOP) is the most important modifiable risk factor, but glaucoma may occur even when measured IOP is within the statistically normal range. Because established glaucomatous damage is generally irreversible, early diagnosis and sustained treatment are essential.This review describes the basic anatomy and physiology of aqueous humour, mechanisms and classification of glaucoma, clinical presentation, diagnostic evaluation and current treatment approaches. Particular attention is given to primary congenital glaucoma and secondary glaucoma. Congenital glaucoma is usually caused by developmental abnormalities of the anterior chamber angle and may lead to corneal enlargement, buphthalmos and optic-nerve damage. metas.titre: Auto-GlaKG: Automated Biomarker Reasoning for Explainable Glaucoma Detection
metas.texte: Auto-GlaKG: Automated Biomarker Reasoning for Explainable Glaucoma Detection. Interpretable glaucoma detection requires a transparent connection between fundus images, clinically meaningful biomarkers, and diagnostic predictions. Knowledge graph (KG) reasoning provides this structure, but performance measured using annotated biomarkers does not establish performance when only images are available. We present Auto-GlaKG, an automated framework that combines image-based biomarker prediction with fixed clinical-prior rules. A ResNet50 network predicts the cup-to-disc ratio (CDR) and six morphological signs using biomarker supervision, and a KG reasoner aggregates their signed rule contributions into a glaucoma score. On 689 fundus images evaluated using stratified, group-aware five-fold cross-validation, Auto-GlaKG achieves a pooled area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.951 (95\% confidence interval: 0.931--0.969), with sensitivity of 0.970 and specificity of 0.779. metas.texte: Lamina Cribrosa Strain as a Glaucoma Prognostic Factor: The STRAIN Study Methodology and Initial Outcomes.
